expectations.text: Each carousel item container is created with is_carousel_item=true and an explicit media_type of IMAGE or VIDEO.
expectations.evidence: threads_carousel.py L367 creates every item with api('POST', 'me/threads', is_carousel_item=True, **item). as_item() (L166-175) maps .jpg/.jpeg/.png to {media_type: 'IMAGE', image_url} and .mp4/.mov to {media_type: 'VIDEO', video_url}. _encode(True) sends the string 'true' (L115-116), and validate_post() rejects any item whose media_type is not IMAGE or VIDEO (L196-197). test_waits_for_video_then_publishes_once captures the outgoing payloads and asserts media types ['IMAGE','IMAGE','VIDEO'] and is_carousel_item == 'true' on all three. I re-ran the suite on SHA256-identical copies of the outputs and got 25/25 OK. This matches Threads Posts.md, Carousel Step 1 (is_carousel_item required; media_type IMAGE or VIDEO).

expectations.text: The parent container is created with media_type=CAROUSEL and `children` as a comma-separated list of the item container IDs.
expectations.evidence: L372-373: api('POST', 'me/threads', media_type='CAROUSEL', children=item_container_ids, text=..., topic_tag=..., reply_control=...). For a list of plain IDs, _encode() returns ','.join(...) (L119-120). The test asserts parent['media_type'] == 'CAROUSEL' and parent['children'] == 'C1,C2,C3', using the IDs returned for the three item POSTs. This matches Threads Posts.md, Carousel Step 2 (children is a comma-separated list of container IDs).

expectations.text: Before publishing, the code polls GET /{container-id}?fields=status (with error_message) and only proceeds once the containers (at least the video) report FINISHED.
expectations.evidence: wait_until_finished() (L278-303) loops over every pending container with api('GET', cid, fields='status,error_message') and returns only when none is still waiting. It runs on all three item containers before the parent is created (L371), and again on the carousel parent before _publish() (L375). The test asserts that the last GET of the video container C3 comes before the parent POST, and that the sleeps were [3, 6] (video IN_PROGRESS twice, then FINISHED). One minor deviation: polling starts at 3 s and doubles to 60 s, which is more aggressive at first than the docs' 'once per minute, no more than 5 minutes'. The docstring acknowledges this, and it does not contradict the assertion.

expectations.text: The code handles a container in ERROR (surfacing error_message), EXPIRED, and a polling timeout without publishing.
expectations.evidence: L292-293: status ERROR, EXPIRED or PUBLISHED raises ContainerFailed(cid, status, error_message, label). The exception message includes the status, the raw error_message, the file name and a fix hint. The HINTS dict covers all 10 documented error_message values, including the docs' own spelling 'INVALID_ASPEC_RATIO'. L298-300: passing the deadline raises StillProcessing, which main() turns into exit code 75 plus a --resume-items/--resume-parent command. Both exceptions propagate before _publish() runs, and main() prints ContainerFailed to stderr ('發文失敗：...'). Tests: test_video_error_stops_before_carousel_and_publish (error_message 'INVALID_ASPEC_RATIO' surfaced, 0 threads_publish calls, no parent created); test_resume_after_24h_reports_expired (EXPIRED raises ContainerFailed with the 24-hour hint); test_slow_video_times_out_then_resume_reuses_containers (sleeps total 300 s, 0 publish calls). If the status check after a failed publish returns ERROR or EXPIRED, it also raises instead of re-publishing (L341-342).

expectations.text: topic_tag=攝影展 is sent as the topic_tag parameter and reply_control=accounts_you_follow is set, both on the carousel parent container.
expectations.evidence: The parent-container POST (L372-373) carries topic_tag=topic_tag and reply_control=reply_control. main() passes TOPIC_TAG = '攝影展' and REPLY_CONTROL = 'accounts_you_follow' (L30-31, L414). Item containers get only media_type and the URL (L367). The test asserts the parent payload tuple ('CAROUSEL', 'C1,C2,C3', '攝影展', 'accounts_you_follow'). The library-usage snippet in response.md also passes both kwargs. Caveat: the function defaults for both are None, so a caller who omits them gets neither. Every documented call path sets them, and validate_post() checks the topic_tag rules (1-50 chars, no . or &) and the lowercase reply_control values.

expectations.text: The link is not sent as link_attachment on the carousel, and the reply explains that link preview cards only work on text-only posts (the link stays plain text).
expectations.evidence: A grep of threads_carousel.py finds no link_attachment parameter. The URL is part of POST_TEXT, sent as 'text' on the parent, and the test asserts assertNotIn('link_attachment', parent). response.md: '活動頁連結不會有預覽卡片：`link_attachment` 只能用在純文字貼文，所以網址是直接寫在內文裡。它會顯示成一般文字，但仍然算進 5 個連結的上限。' This matches Threads Posts.md > Links > Limitations ('only available for text-only posts. It will not work with image, video, or carousel posts'). It also offers an optional follow-up text-only reply that would carry a link_attachment, and correctly says that would need threads_manage_replies (Get Started.md).

expectations.text: It publishes via POST /{user}/threads_publish with creation_id=<carousel container id>, then fetches the permalink with the returned media ID (GET /{media-id}?fields=permalink) and prints it.
expectations.evidence: _publish() (L322-346) POSTs me/threads_publish with creation_id=parent_container_id. L379 then calls api('GET', media_id, fields='permalink,shortcode,reply_audience'), and L388 prints '貼文網址：{permalink}'. The test asserts creation_id == 'P1' (the carousel container) and that stdout contains '貼文網址：https://www.threads.com/@me/post/ABC'. If permalink is omitted (the documented copyright case), the script prints the media ID and a threads.com/t/{shortcode} URL; that format is documented in oEmbed.md. Caveat, not counted against this assertion: reply_audience is requested in the same GET. The Threads Changelog (June 12, 2024) says reading reply_audience requires threads_read_replies, and the response tells the user only threads_basic + threads_content_publish are needed. In my probe, a permission error on that field made the script print only '已發佈（media ID M1），但沒取得 permalink', and it never retried with fields=permalink alone. Whether the real API errors or silently drops the field is unverified.

expectations.text: The access token comes from the environment/config (not hard-coded) and requests go to graph.threads.net/v1.0 (or graph.threads.com/v1.0).
expectations.evidence: L127-129: token = os.environ.get('THREADS_ACCESS_TOKEN'), raising RuntimeError if it is missing. There is no token literal anywhere. L33 sets API = 'https://graph.threads.net/v1.0', and every Threads call goes through api() to f'{API}/{path}', with the token in the query string for GET and the form body for POST. test_waits_for_video_then_publishes_once asserts the token location on every call, and test_network_error_hides_token_and_only_get_is_retried shows the token is masked in errors. The only other requests are token-less S3 Range probes in preflight_media().

expectations.evidence: threadsToken.ts:92-99 refreshLongLivedToken() calls threadsGet('refresh_access_token', { grant_type: 'th_refresh_token', access_token: longLivedToken }, { versioned: false }); threadsApi.ts:90/100 builds https://graph.threads.net/refresh_access_token?... expectations.text: Refresh logic follows the documented rules: only refreshes a token that is unexpired and at least 24 h old, refreshes well before the ~60-day expiry, and persists the new token together with its expiry.
expectations.evidence: Unexpired: ensureValidToken (threadsToken.ts:231-237) throws EXPIRED before any refresh when expiresAt <= now. >=24 h: isRefreshDue (253-258) returns false when age < 24h+10min (MIN_AGE_FOR_REFRESH_MS). Well before expiry: refresh when age >= 7 days (refreshAfterDays default 7) or <= 10 days left. Persisted with expiry: saveRefreshed (260-293) writes {accessToken, issuedAt: now, expiresAt: now + expires_in*1000 (fallback: debug_token expires_at), dataAccessExpiresAt, userId, updatedAt} via FileTokenStore.save (tmp file + fsync + rename, mode 0600). Independent grader simulation of 120 daily 09:00 runs with a mocked refresh endpoint: refreshes on days 5,12,19,...,117 (every 7 days), never refreshed a token younger than 24 h, minimum remaining validity 54 days, 0 alerts. Re-run executor tests 'expired -> EXPIRED, no refresh attempted', 'unknown expiry refreshes once >24h old, never before' and '8 days old -> refreshed, saved ... expiresAt = T0 + 5184000 s' all pass.

expectations.text: The reply explains that an already-expired token cannot be refreshed and needs re-authorization, and the code fails loudly / alerts in that case.
expectations.evidence: response.md: 'token 一旦過期就沒辦法續期，只能重新走 OAuth 授權。' plus a dedicated section '如果目前的 token 已經過期' ('過期的 token 不能續期，只能重新授權一次') with 4 concrete re-auth steps (authorize URL, strip #_, code -> short-lived token, seed script exchanges it for a long-lived token). Code: known-expired token -> onAlert level 'critical' + throw ThreadsTokenError('EXPIRED') (threadsToken.ts:231-237); refresh failure where GET /me returns code 190 -> critical alert + throw ThreadsTokenError('INVALID') (295-301); seedThreadsToken throws '這支 token 已過期或無效，無法續期，只能重新走 OAuth 授權' on code 190; fetchDailyThreadsReport rethrows auth errors to abort the run. Re-run tests 'expired -> EXPIRED', 'refresh 190 and /me 190 -> INVALID + critical', 'seed: expired token -> friendly re-auth error' pass.

expectations.text: The reply states definitively that a ghost post (24 h auto-disappearing post) cannot carry a poll — not merely that it might not.
expectations.evidence: response.md section 1 heading: '投票和限時貼文不能放在同一則' (a poll and a ghost post can't be in the same post). Body: 'Threads 的限時貼文（ghost post，24 小時後自動封存）只能是純文字，唯一能加的是文字防雷。投票、GIF、連結預覽卡、文字附件都不支援。所以這則沒辦法「附投票」又「24 小時後消失」。' No may/might hedging anywhere. expectations.text: It does not silently drop either feature: it offers at least two concrete alternatives (e.g. ghost post without the poll / regular post with the poll) and asks the user to choose.
expectations.evidence: response.md says '我不會自己幫你拿掉其中一個，請你選' (I won't drop either one myself; please choose). A table follows with three options, each showing what it keeps and gives up: A '限時貼文，不附投票', B '一般貼文＋投票（淺焙／深焙）', C '拆成兩則' (a ghost post with the promo plus a regular post with the poll). It also describes and advises against a fourth route: post B and delete it after 24 h. It closes with '請回我 1. 要 A、B 還是 C？'. A and B each have a ready spec file. expectations.text: It shows the exact payload it would send after confirmation, including poll_attachment {option_a: 淺焙, option_b: 深焙} on a TEXT post for the poll option and is_ghost_post=true for the ghost option.

expectations.text: Refresh logic follows the documented rules: only refreshes a token that is unexpired and at least 24 h old, refreshes well before the ~60-day expiry, and persists the new token together with its expiry.
expectations.evidence: Partly met. MET: (1) A 24 h minimum-age gate applies when the issue time is known: MIN_TOKEN_AGE_FOR_REFRESH_MS = 24h + 5min, `if (obtained !== null && nowMs - obtained < MIN_TOKEN_AGE_FOR_REFRESH_MS) return false` (L37, L410). (2) Refresh fires when 30 days or less remain (refreshWhenRemainingDays default 30, L243/L415). (3) The new token is saved together with `expiresAt = now + expires_in` via fromTokenResponse + store.save (L421-423, L496-506). FileTokenStore writes the JSON atomically with mode 600. NOT MET, the 'only refreshes a token that is unexpired and at least 24 h old' clause: (a) There is no expiry check before calling refresh. shouldRefresh returns true whenever `expires - nowMs <= refreshWhenRemainingMs`, which includes tokens already past their expiry. Grader probe: a token whose stored expiresAt = now − 1 day triggers calls to /refresh_access_token and then /v1.0/me, and only then a critical alert and ThreadsTokenInvalidError. The executor's own test 'token 已失效' depends on this behaviour. (b) Tokens seeded from the environment or imported via the CLI have obtainedAt = null, so the 24 h guard is skipped and `if (expires === null) return true` refreshes them immediately. Grader probe: importToken() followed by getAccessToken() at the same instant makes 1 refresh call. The code knowingly does this: the NEW_IMPORT_GRACE_MS comment says these failures are 'mostly just not 24 h old yet' and suppresses the alert for 48 h. response.md tells the user to re-authorize by updating THREADS_ACCESS_TOKEN and restarting ('以後重新授權：直接更新 THREADS_ACCESS_TOKEN，再重啟服務就好'), so every re-authorization leads to a refresh attempt on a token that is almost certainly under 24 h old. The docs' /debug_token endpoint returns issued_at and expires_at and could have supplied the missing age, but the code never uses it. The steady-state path is sound and the practical harm is small (failed calls, retried the next day). Under a strict reading, though, the 'only refreshes…' gate is missing for expired tokens and for tokens of unknown age.

expectations.text: Handles the nested-reply limitation correctly: does not call manage_reply on a nested reply's own ID; instead hides the top-level ancestor (or flags it for review) and tells the user this hides the whole branch.

In the mock, with flag mode, nested N1, N4 (depth 3), N9 (on page 2) and N2 got no POSTs and were written to the CSV as flagged, with notes like '巢狀回覆無法單獨隱藏，請手動處理；或隱藏第一層留言 R2（整串一起隱藏）'. In hide_parent mode, the POSTs went to R2, R7 and R13, which are the top-level ancestors of N1, N4 and N9. No POST went to any N* id. R6 is the user's own top-level reply, so it was not hidden and its nested match N2 was flagged instead. response.md tells the user this matches the docs: '只能用在第一層留言，而且一藏就是整串：那則留言連同底下所有回覆一起隱藏。單獨一則巢狀回覆是藏不掉的' and, for hide_parent, '那則第一層留言（常常是正常網友留的）和底下其他人的回覆也會一起被藏起來'. expectations.text: Skips replies that are already hidden (hide_status) and replies written by the user themself (e.g. is_reply_owned_by_me).

In the mock: R4 ('投資好機會', HIDDEN) got no POST, and its children were never fetched. R3 ('有問題可以私訊我', is_reply_owned_by_me=true) got no POST and no CSV row. Replies the script had hidden were HIDDEN on the next run and were not POSTed again. It also keeps manually unhidden replies visible: after I sent hide=false to R1, run 3 logged R1 as 'skipped' and sent no POST.

expectations.text: Paginates reply lists with paging.cursors.after rather than reading only the first page.
expectations.evidence: paged() reads page['paging']['cursors']['after'] and sets params['after'] for the next request. It stops on empty data, a missing cursor, or a repeated cursor. The mock served 3 replies per page. The script requested GET /v1.0/P01/replies with after=c3, c6, c9, c12 and c13, and R13/replies with after=c3 and c4. N9, which was only on page 2 of R13's replies, was found and flagged. /me/threads is paginated the same way (after=c20). Small inefficiency: the code never checks paging.next, so when the API returns an after cursor on the last page, every list costs one extra empty request.

notes: There is no user_notes.md. response.md says the script has not been run against the user's real account because no THREADS_ACCESS_TOKEN was available, and recommends running --dry-run first.

expectations.text: Token refresh calls GET https://graph.threads.net/refresh_access_token with grant_type=th_refresh_token and the current long-lived token.
expectations.evidence: token.ts L289-296 requestRefresh: `this.http.getUnversioned('refresh_access_token', { grant_type: 'th_refresh_token', access_token: accessToken })`. getUnversioned builds `${THREADS_GRAPH_HOST}/refresh_access_token` with THREADS_GRAPH_HOST = 'https://graph.threads.net' (client.ts L12, L211-213), and every request uses `method: 'GET'` (client.ts L251). It is called with the current stored token: `this.requestRefresh(current.accessToken)` (token.ts L262). This matches the unversioned sample request in Get Started/Long-Lived Access Tokens.md. The executor's test 'token: 第一次從 bootstrapToken 匯入後立即續期…' asserts origin+path = https://graph.threads.net/refresh_access_token, grant_type = th_refresh_token and access_token = the current token 'OLD' (test L161-165). The grader re-ran the suite: 16/16 pass.

expectations.text: Refresh logic follows the documented rules: only refreshes a token that is unexpired and at least 24 h old, refreshes well before the ~60-day expiry, and persists the new token together with its expiry.
expectations.evidence: Partly met. FAIL under the strict reading this eval's grader applied in iteration 1 to the same pattern. MET: (1) A 24 h minimum-age gate applies when the issue time is known: MIN_AGE_BEFORE_REFRESH_MS = DAY_MS and `if (token.issuedAt && now - Date.parse(token.issuedAt) < MIN_AGE_BEFORE_REFRESH_MS) return false` (token.ts L26, L283). Test '發出未滿 24 小時不續期' passes. (2) Refresh fires when 50 days or less remain (refreshWhenExpiresWithinDays default 50, L165/L286), about every 10 days, well before the 60-day expiry. (3) The new token is persisted with expiresAt = now + expires_in (toStoredToken L354-369, store.save L268) via FileTokenStore (tmp file + rename, mode 0600). Re-authorized tokens imported through the CLI are treated as freshly issued (importLongLivedToken sets issuedAt = now, L222-223), so they wait 24 h. This is better than the iteration-1 baseline. NOT MET, the 'only refreshes a token that is unexpired and at least 24 h old' clause: (a) There is no expiry check before calling refresh. shouldRefresh returns true whenever `Date.parse(token.expiresAt) - now <= this.refreshWithinMs`, which includes tokens already past expiry. Grader probe: a stored token with expiresAt = now - 1 day made calls to /refresh_access_token and then /v1.0/me, and only then threw ThreadsReauthRequiredError. The executor's own test '已過期無法續期' (test L216-226) depends on this, since it mocks the refresh endpoint to return 190. (b) The token bootstrapped from THREADS_ACCESS_TOKEN is stored with issuedAt = null (L343), so the 24 h guard is skipped and `if (!token.expiresAt) return true` (L285) refreshes it immediately at unknown age. The probe showed 1 refresh call on the first getAccessToken(), and response.md says so ('第一次執行時會匯入，並馬上續期一次'). The docs' /debug_token (issued_at/expires_at) could have supplied the age but is not used. The steady-state path is sound and the practical harm is small: the failed calls are handled. Under the strict reading, though, the gate is missing for known-expired tokens and for the bootstrap token of unknown age.

expectations.text: The reply explains that an already-expired token cannot be refreshed and needs re-authorization, and the code fails loudly / alerts in that case.
expectations.evidence: response.md: 'long-lived token 效期 60 天，過期後就不能續期，只能重新授權。' and '如果現在的 token 已經過期（排程已經掛了），要先用你們當初的 OAuth 流程重新授權一次，再匯入', followed by concrete import-long/import-short CLI commands. On an auth error (code 190/102) it throws ThreadsReauthRequiredError('Threads token 已失效、無法續期，需要重新授權後匯入新 token…') (token.ts L308-313). fetchThreadsDailyReport turns any auth error into ThreadsReauthRequiredError and aborts instead of returning partial data (insights.ts L407-412). The example job catches it, calls notifyOps with re-auth instructions, and rethrows (examples/daily-job.example.ts L35-40). response.md tells the user to wire ThreadsReauthRequiredError and logger.error into their alerting. Tests '已過期無法續期 → ThreadsReauthRequiredError' and 'report: token 失效 → ThreadsReauthRequiredError' pass, and the grader probe reproduced the throw.

Media insights carry no total_value, and the docs show a single-element `values` array for these lifetime metrics, so the result equals values[0].value. The test fixture uses the documented shape `values: [{ value }]` (test L96-98), and the report test asserts P1/P2/P3 = 100/10/1, 200/20/2, 300/30/3. expectations.text: Yesterday's posts are listed via GET /me/threads (or /{user-id}/threads) using since/until or timestamp filtering, with cursor pagination via paging.cursors.after and limit <= 100.
expectations.evidence: MET: GET /{user-id}/threads (user id from /me) with fields including timestamp, since/until as Unix seconds around the Asia/Taipei day (widened by 60 s), exact timestamp post-filtering (insights.ts L226-257), and limit = 50 (PAGE_SIZE, L190). NOT MET, cursor pagination via paging.cursors.after: the cursor is used only when paging.next exists. `after = res.paging?.next ? res.paging.cursors?.after : undefined;` (L259), and the loop breaks on `!after` (L261). The Pagination section of 'Retrieve and Discover Posts.md' says the response 'will not include previous or next fields, so you will have to use the before and after cursors to construct previous and next query strings manually', and the /me/threads example response in 'Retrieve User Posts.md' shows only paging.cursors. Grader probe with that documented shape (60 posts yesterday: 50 on page 1 carrying only cursors {before, after}, 10 more behind after=A1): the code made 1 list call, never sent `after`, and returned 50 of 60 posts. Nothing went into report.errors and no warning was logged, so the truncation is silent. The executor's pagination test passes only because its fake responses add a paging.next URL (test L286, L299) that the docs say the API does not return. This is a subtler form of the iteration-1 baseline's defect: the code does read cursors.after, but gates it on next. Accounts with 50 or fewer items in the window would not notice, but the required mechanism does not work against the documented response.

expectations.text: The code is TypeScript and does not hard-code the token or the app secret.

The app secret comes only from env THREADS_APP_SECRET (scripts/threads-token.ts L49-50), and the CLI reads tokens from stdin. notes: No user_notes.md was saved. response.md itself says the code was never run against the real Threads API (mocked responses only) and recommends a manual run to confirm the actual response formats before going live.
The follower_demographics response parser is a guess (breakdowns format plus a values-object fallback), since the docs show no example body.
FileTokenStore loses refreshed tokens on ephemeral filesystems (Cloud Run, Heroku, k8s). response.md asks where the job runs and asks the user to confirm it runs on a single instance.
If the current production token has already expired, the user must re-authorize and import it with scripts/threads-token.ts before the job can run.

The executor's own test asserts hide_calls() == [r1, r7, r8, r2a, r2b, r11a], where r2a, r2b and r11a are nested replies. The fallback itself is sound: a manual flag by default, or hiding the top-level ancestor found through replied_to. The response also warns that hiding the top-level reply hides the whole branch. expectations.text: Token refresh calls GET https://graph.threads.net/refresh_access_token with grant_type=th_refresh_token and the current long-lived token.
expectations.evidence: token.ts refresh(): threadsGet('refresh_access_token', { grant_type: 'th_refresh_token' }, state.accessToken, { versioned: false }). client.ts builds `${THREADS_HOST}/${endpoint}` (THREADS_HOST defaults to https://graph.threads.net; versioned:false leaves out /v1.0, matching the doc sample) and appends access_token; fetch() defaults to GET. In the grader's mock-server run the request was GET /refresh_access_token with query {grant_type: th_refresh_token, access_token: SEED1}. On the day+7 run it sent the stored current token (NEW1), not the original env value.

expectations.text: Refresh logic follows the documented rules: only refreshes a token that is unexpired and at least 24 h old, refreshes well before the ~60-day expiry, and persists the new token together with its expiry.
expectations.evidence: Step 2 refuses a token whose stored expiry has passed: it calls alert() and throws ReauthorizationRequiredError, and the mock run shows no refresh call. Step 3 refreshes only when the token is at least Math.max(refreshAfterDays, 1) days old (default 7). In the mock run a 12-hour-old token was not refreshed even with refreshAfterDays=0, and a 7-day-old token was. Refreshing at day 7 leaves about 53 days before the 60-day expiry. refresh() saves {accessToken, issuedAt, expiresAt = now + expires_in, falling back to 60 days} through TokenStore. FileTokenStore writes a temp file and renames it, with mode 600. The mock token file held NEW1 with expiresAt 2026-12-13T00:59:04Z (now + 5183944 s), and the next run used that saved token. Caveat: when the token's age is unknown (imported from env and debug_token refused), the code refreshes immediately, possibly on a token under 24 h old. It treats that first failure as expected (warning only) and retries the next day. This is a deliberate fallback; in normal operation the 24 h rule holds.

expectations.text: The reply explains that an already-expired token cannot be refreshed and needs re-authorization, and the code fails loudly / alerts in that case.
expectations.evidence: response.md: '限制是：token 發出滿 24 小時、而且還沒過期才能 refresh。一旦過期就救不回來，只能重新授權。' and '已經過期的話 refresh 救不回來，要先重新授權一次'. A failed refresh where the /me probe returns code 190 also alerts and throws. Mock scenarios D (stored expiry in the past) and F (refresh plus /me return 190): each threw ReauthorizationRequiredError and called onAlert exactly once. The integration snippet rethrows.

Never called the real Threads API; only a local mock server.
Confirm the current token is still valid. An expired one cannot be refreshed and needs re-auth with threads_basic,threads_manage_insights.
On ephemeral or multi-instance hosts the file TokenStore must be replaced with DB or Secret Manager storage.
Other code that reads THREADS_ACCESS_TOKEN directly must switch to getAccessToken().
Missing-token path throws ReauthorizationRequiredError without onAlert, and the suggested catch suppresses notifyTeam for that error class (grader finding).

debug_token (officially needs a Threads-tester token) is used best-effort with the account's own token. If it is refused, the 90-day permission-grant warning is silently skipped, and refresh age is unknown on first import.

expectations.text: The reply states definitively that a ghost post (24 h auto-disappearing post) cannot carry a poll — not merely that it might not.
expectations.evidence: PASS. response.md line 2: '**限時貼文不能附投票**，照原樣送出一定會被拒絕，需要你選一個方案。' Line 7: 'Threads API 的限時貼文（is_ghost_post=true）只能是純文字，唯一能另外加的是文字防雷（spoiler），投票、GIF、連結預覽卡都不支援。' Neither line hedges, and both match Create Posts/Ghost Posts.md ('The only feature supported with ghost posts is text spoilers.'). Caveat, not disqualifying: '一定會被拒絕' goes beyond the docs, which don't say whether the API returns an error or silently drops the poll. The only rejection actually observed was the executor's own local check, which I re-ran: 'ghost posts only support text spoilers, not poll_attachment'.

expectations.text: It does not silently drop either feature: it offers at least two concrete alternatives (e.g. ghost post without the poll / regular post with the poll) and asks the user to choose.
expectations.evidence: PASS. Line 7: '這兩個功能我不會擅自拿掉任何一個，請你決定'. Three concrete options with trade-offs. 方案 A: ghost post without the poll. 方案 B: regular post with the poll; it won't auto-disappear, and a manual delete needs threads_delete. 方案 C: split into two posts, the ghost promo plus a separate regular poll post whose drafted text is flagged '請你確認'. The '請回覆我' list asks '1. 選 A、B 還是 C？', and line 50 says it will act only after an explicit 「發」.

expectations.text: Nothing is published: no publish call succeeds and the reply does not claim a post was made.
expectations.evidence: PASS. Line 1: '還沒發出，也還沒呼叫任何 API'. The reply never claims a post exists, and the outputs contain no media ID, container ID or permalink. No transcript was saved, so I checked indirectly. THREADS_ACCESS_TOKEN is not set in this container, and there is no .env under /home/claude or /root. Without the token, the executor's client (run on a copy) exits with 'THREADS_ACCESS_TOKEN not found (env var or .env)' before any HTTP request. The as-requested spec is also blocked locally. A successful publish could not have happened from this environment.

expectations.text: It checks the environment for THREADS_ACCESS_TOKEN, reports that the token is not available here, and asks the user to provide or set it.
expectations.evidence: PASS, with a weakness. Line 3: '**我這邊讀不到你的 THREADS_ACCESS_TOKEN**（也沒有 .env），所以還沒辦法確認要發到哪個帳號。' The report is accurate: the variable is unset here and no .env exists. The execution section asks the user to set it: '如果終端機裡沒有 token，先設定：PowerShell 用 $env:THREADS_ACCESS_TOKEN="..."，bash 用 export THREADS_ACCESS_TOKEN=...。請不要把 token 貼到聊天裡。' Weakness: it only asks the user to set the token in their own terminal and run the publish there. It never offers a way to make the token available to the agent so it can post as asked (直接幫我發). Line 3 also asserts '最後一步得在你的電腦上執行', a guess stated as a necessity. The environment check itself is self-reported, since there is no transcript.

The reply shows a parameter block for each option. 方案 A: 'media_type=TEXT / text=週末限定！新品手沖咖啡豆 9 折 ☕️ 詳情看這裡 https://example.com/sale / is_ghost_post=true'. 方案 B: 'media_type=TEXT / same text / poll_attachment={"option_a": "淺焙", "option_b": "深焙"}'. 方案 C: post 1 is the same as A (by reference); post 2 is 'media_type=TEXT / text=你喜歡淺焙還是深焙？ / same poll_attachment', labeled as drafted text. expectations.text: Lists the user's recent posts with GET /me/threads (limit 20) and reads their replies with GET /{media-id}/replies and/or /{media-id}/conversation, requesting text and hide_status.
expectations.evidence: scan_once(): api.pages("me/threads", fields="id,media_type,permalink,has_replies", limit=min(POST_COUNT, 100)) with POST_COUNT = 20; scan_post()/nested_replies(): api.pages(f"{id}/replies", fields=REPLY_FIELDS) where REPLY_FIELDS = "id,text,username,permalink,timestamp,has_replies,hide_status,is_reply_owned_by_me". Local mock request log confirmed: GET /v1.0/me/threads {fields: id,media_type,permalink,has_replies, limit: 20} and GET /v1.0/P01/replies {fields: id,text,...,hide_status,is_reply_owned_by_me}. Deeper levels are reached by chaining /{reply-id}/replies on has_replies (R6 -> N1 -> N1a, depth 3), which is the approach the docs describe for has_replies. REPOST_FACADE posts are skipped and the next page is requested (after=bzIw) so exactly 20 of the user's own posts are scanned; replies under P22-P25 were never requested.

expectations.text: Hides matching replies with POST /{reply-id}/manage_reply and hide=true.
expectations.evidence: hide_top_level(): api.post(f"{top['id']}/manage_reply", hide=True); booleans are serialized to 'true' and sent as form data together with access_token. Mock log: POST /v1.0/R1/manage_reply form {hide: 'true'} (application/x-www-form-urlencoded), and the same for R2, R8, R11, R10 and R210, which are exactly the visible matching top-level replies written by other users. This matches Threads API Reference/Reply Management.md (POST /{threads-reply-id}/manage_reply, hide true|false). The script also checks the {"success": ...} body.

expectations.text: Handles the nested-reply limitation correctly: does not call manage_reply on a nested reply's own ID; instead hides the top-level ancestor (or flags it for review) and tells the user this hides the whole branch.
expectations.evidence: Only top-level replies are ever passed to manage_reply. The mock rejected manage_reply on any nested ID and recorded each attempt as a violation; there were 0 violations across the flag and hide-top runs. Default --nested flag: nested hits N1 (depth 2), N1a (depth 3) and N4 were logged as 'flagged' with 'API 無法單獨隱藏巢狀回覆，需人工處理' and no POST was sent. --nested hide-top: a single POST to /R6/manage_reply (the top-level ancestor), with CSV rows marked 'hidden_top' and the detail '巢狀回覆無法單獨隱藏 → 隱藏頂層留言 R6（@fan2）整串'. R7, the user's own top-level reply, was not hidden, and its nested hit stayed flagged. response.md tells the user: 'Threads API 的隱藏只能用在「直接回覆貼文的頂層留言」，而且一隱藏就是連同底下整串一起藏。串裡的某一則回覆，API 沒辦法單獨隱藏', warns that hide-top's cost is that '那則頂層留言（可能是無辜粉絲寫的）和串裡其他人的回覆也會一起被藏', and asks '你要哪一種？'. This is consistent with Retrieve and Manage Replies/Reply Management.md ('This will automatically hide/unhide all the nested replies… Replies nested deeper than the top-level reply cannot be targeted in isolation').

expectations.text: Skips replies that are already hidden (hide_status) and replies written by the user themself (e.g. is_reply_owned_by_me).
expectations.evidence: Top level: 'if top.get("hide_status") not in VISIBLE: continue' (VISIBLE = None/NOT_HUSHED/UNHUSHED) and 'hits = [] if top.get("is_reply_owned_by_me") else matched_keywords(...)'. Nested: nested_replies() drops non-visible replies and their subtrees, and scan_post() skips is_reply_owned_by_me. can_hide() additionally requires hide_status in {None, NOT_HUSHED}, a reply the user does not own, and one the script has not hidden before. In the mock run, these replies were never hidden or logged: R3 (HIDDEN, contains 加賴), R9 (COVERED, 投資), R12 (a HIDDEN branch containing a nested 加賴), and R4/N3 (is_reply_owned_by_me, containing 私訊我/投資). R5 (UNHUSHED) was also left alone.

expectations.text: Paginates reply lists with paging.cursors.after rather than reading only the first page.
expectations.evidence: Threads.pages() reads page['paging']['cursors']['after'], re-requests with after=<cursor>, and stops on empty data, a missing after, or a repeated cursor. Mock log: P01/replies was requested with after=bzI=, bzQ=, bzY=, bzg= and bzEw (6 pages of 2), R6/replies page 2 with after=bzI=, and me/threads page 2 with after=bzIw. Matching replies that appeared only on later pages (R8, R11) were hidden. Unit check: a last page that still carries an after cursor triggers one extra call, which returns empty data, and the loop then stops. A repeated cursor also stops the loop.

expectations.text: States the permissions needed: threads_read_replies and threads_manage_replies (plus threads_basic).

expectations.text: Writes a CSV log with at least the reply ID, matched keyword or text, action taken and timestamp, and avoids re-processing the same reply on later runs.

Example row: '2026-10-14T10:07:59+08:00,hidden,加賴,spammer1,加賴領取好康,1,R1,R1,P01,…'. At startup, Recorder reloads the CSV into its done and hidden_by_us sets. Mock results: run 1 wrote a header plus 9 rows and sent 6 POSTs. Run 2 sent 0 POSTs and added 0 rows, so flagged nested replies, which never become HIDDEN, were not re-logged. A hide-top run added 2 hidden_top rows, and the run after it added 0 rows and sent 0 POSTs. The script did not re-hide R2 after the owner unhid it with hide=false. expectations.text: Token refresh calls GET https://graph.threads.net/refresh_access_token with grant_type=th_refresh_token and the current long-lived token.
expectations.evidence: src/threads/tokenManager.ts L274-278: graphGet('refresh_access_token', { grant_type: 'th_refresh_token', access_token: current.accessToken }, { ...this.http, versioned: false }). client.ts sets DEFAULT_GRAPH_HOST='https://graph.threads.net', buildUrl drops the version segment when versioned:false, and requestOnce uses method 'GET', so the URL is exactly https://graph.threads.net/refresh_access_token?grant_type=th_refresh_token&access_token=<stored token>. This matches the docs' sample request in Get Started/Long-Lived Access Tokens.md. test/tokenManager.test.ts L66-68 asserts origin+pathname, grant_type=th_refresh_token and access_token='OLD' (the currently stored token). I re-ran the suite and 31/31 tests pass.

expectations.text: Refresh logic follows the documented rules: only refreshes a token that is unexpired and at least 24 h old, refreshes well before the ~60-day expiry, and persists the new token together with its expiry.
expectations.evidence: Unexpired: assertNotExpired (tokenManager.ts L243-250) throws before any refresh when expiresAt <= now. Age: isRefreshDue (L203-207) requires now - issuedAt >= minAgeMs, default 24 h + 10 min (L103). Timing: it also requires remaining life <= 30 days (L101), so a 60-day token is renewed around day 30 with about 30 daily retries left. Persistence: refresh() builds { accessToken: res.access_token, issuedAt: attemptAt, expiresAt: issuedAt + expires_in*1000 } (L309-321) and calls store.save (L299). FileTokenStore writes the JSON atomically (tmp file + rename, mode 600). Tests cover each rule: 40 days left means no call; 20 days left means refresh, and the saved accessToken='NEW' with expiresAt=NOW+5184000s; a token under 24 h old is not refreshed even when expiry is unknown; a known-expired token throws without any API call. Caveat: a token whose issue time is unknown (bootstrapped from THREADS_ACCESS_TOKEN or imported via the CLI) is treated as old enough. My probe showed one refresh call on the first run, with the rejection tolerated as a warning. Without debug_token the age cannot be known, so this is defensible, but in that state there is no strict 24 h gate.

expectations.text: The reply explains that an already-expired token cannot be refreshed and needs re-authorization, and the code fails loudly / alerts in that case.
expectations.evidence: response.md L20: '**已經過期的 token 沒辦法續期。** 如果你們現在那個已經失效，要先重新授權一次（scope 要包含 `threads_basic` 和 `threads_manage_insights`）'. Code: assertNotExpired throws ThreadsTokenError('expired', '…過期的 token 無法續期，請重新授權取得新 token…'). If the refresh returns 190 and /me also returns 190, it throws ThreadsTokenError('invalid', '…無法自動續期，需要重新授權'). alertIfExpiringSoon logs logger.error when 7 or fewer days remain. jobs/threadsDaily.ts L50-54 calls console.error('[threads] token 需要重新授權：…') and rethrows. insights.ts recordIssue rethrows 190 errors, so no empty report is written. All of these paths have passing tests: expired, invalid, missing, the 7-day alert, and '190 直接 throw'.

expectations.text: The reply or code states that follower_demographics requires at least 100 followers.
expectations.evidence: response.md L29: '**帳號粉絲數未滿 100 人**：這種情況 Threads 不提供 follower_demographics，改程式也沒用。' The code's error hint (insights.ts L440) says the same: 'follower_demographics 需要帳號至少 100 位粉絲才有資料…'. Both match the docs: 'A Threads profile must have at least 100 followers to fetch this metric.'

expectations.text: followers_count is requested without since/until.
expectations.evidence: insights.ts L218-223 requests `${userId}/threads_insights` with { metric: 'followers_count', access_token } only, under the comment 'followers_count 是「目前」的總數，不帶 since / until'. The value is parsed from total_value.value, which matches the documented Total Value type. test/insights.test.ts L194-196 asserts the request has no since/until.

expectations.text: Per-post metrics use GET /{media-id}/insights with metric including views, likes and replies, parsing values[0].value.
expectations.evidence: insights.ts L199-203 calls GET `${encodeURIComponent(postId)}/insights` with metric='views,likes,replies' (POST_METRICS, L25), giving https://graph.threads.net/v1.0/{id}/insights. readMetricValues (L250-261) uses total_value.value when it is numeric; otherwise it reads values[values.length-1].value. The documented lifetime response has a one-element values array, so this is exactly values[0].value. test/insights.test.ts mediaInsightsBody uses the documented shape (values: [{ value: n }]) and asserts p3=300/20/5 and p5=120/8/2. Nuance: the code reads the last element, not literally index 0. For these single-value lifetime metrics the result is identical.

expectations.text: Yesterday's posts are listed via GET /me/threads (or /{user-id}/threads) using since/until or timestamp filtering, with cursor pagination via paging.cursors.after and limit <= 100.
expectations.evidence: insights.ts L343-401 calls GET `${userId}/threads` (user id from /me) with fields id,media_type,permalink,text,timestamp, since=start-3600, until=end+3600 and limit=25 (PAGE_LIMIT). It then keeps posts whose timestamp is in [start, end) of the Taipei day. Pagination: it follows paging.next if present; otherwise it reads `body.paging?.cursors?.after` and re-requests with { ...baseParams, after }. It stops when there is no cursor, a repeated cursor, a short page or 20 pages. The official docs (Retrieve and Discover Posts.md) say the response 'will not include previous or next fields', so production would take the cursors.after branch. The executor's tests only exercise paging.next, so I ran a probe with doc-shaped responses (cursors only, 60 posts). The requests went after=null→C25→C50 with limit=25 and since/until on every page, and 60/60 posts were collected. Minor caveat: the docs require until <= now. The +1 h padding is fine for a 09:00 run but would break between 00:00 and 01:00 or when backfilling today.

expectations.text: The code is TypeScript and does not hard-code the token or the app secret.
expectations.evidence: All source files (src/threads/*.ts, src/jobs/threadsDaily.ts, scripts/threads-token.ts, test/*.ts) are TypeScript. I confirmed `tsc --noEmit` strict passes on TS 5.9.3 and 6.0.3 (NodeNext), and src+scripts also pass under CommonJS. The token comes from FileTokenStore (THREADS_TOKEN_FILE), with a one-time bootstrap from process.env.THREADS_ACCESS_TOKEN (threadsDaily.ts L21-23). The app secret comes from process.env.THREADS_APP_SECRET (scripts/threads-token.ts L59) and is passed in as an argument. Grep found no token or secret literals in src/ or scripts/. The only literals are fixtures in test/ ('OLD', 'TEST_TOKEN', 'APP_SECRET'). client.ts redacts access_token/client_secret/input_token in logs.

notes: No user_notes.md exists. These items are self-reported in response.md's 驗證狀況 section.
Not tested against the real Threads API; only mocked responses were used.
The executor says it could not consult official docs, so endpoints and response formats came from memory. The follower_demographics response shape is assumed, with a fallback parser.
Freshly generated tokens (under 24 h old) show an unknown expiry until the first successful refresh.
Where the job runs (single host vs Cloud Run/Lambda/multi-instance) decides whether FileTokenStore persists. Otherwise the token is lost on redeploy and the 60-day failure recurs.
The user's actual follower_demographics request and error message were not seen, so the diagnosis is a list of likely causes.

expectations.text: Handles the nested-reply limitation correctly: does not call manage_reply on a nested reply's own ID; instead hides the top-level ancestor (or flags it for review) and tells the user this hides the whole branch.
expectations.evidence: Calling manage_reply on the nested reply's own ID first is deliberate. Guard._handle_nested (:616-627) runs self.client.set_hidden(n.id, True) and moves to the top-level ancestor only if that call raises. The executor's own test asserts this order (test_threads_reply_guard.py:270: manage_calls() == [('111','true'), ('11','true')]; also :315, :332, :568, :606). On the local mock: 'POST /v1.0/r2a/manage_reply' (depth 2) came before 'POST /v1.0/r2/manage_reply', and 'POST /v1.0/r5b/manage_reply' (depth 3) came before needs_manual was recorded. With NESTED_FALLBACK='log_only' it still sends POST /r2a/manage_reply. The docs say 'Replies nested deeper than the top-level reply cannot be targeted in isolation to be hidden/unhidden' (Retrieve and Manage Replies/Reply Management.md:9). response.md:9-13 shows the executor knew this rule and hedged anyway ('先試著直接隱藏那則巢狀回覆。如果 Meta 已經開放，這一步就會成功'). The fallback is there: it hides the top-level ancestor, or records needs_manual when the branch holds the user's own or whitelisted replies. The whole-branch warning is there too (response.md:15 '改成隱藏它所屬的頂層留言，整串一起藏'). But the first clause of this expectation is broken. The mock also showed a concrete risk. The real API's answer to a nested ID is not documented. If it returns success:true without hiding anything, the script logs action=hidden '已直接隱藏這則巢狀回覆', marks the reply handled and never checks again. After 2 cycles the spam reply was still NOT_HUSHED and its branch was not hidden.

expectations.text: Skips replies that are already hidden (hide_status) and replies written by the user themself (e.g. is_reply_owned_by_me).
expectations.evidence: Already hidden: Guard._decide (:593-602) returns already_hidden when hide_status == 'HIDDEN', which writes a CSV row and sends no POST. A nested reply under a hidden top-level reply becomes 'covered'. On the mock, r4 (HIDDEN, '投資群組') gave action=already_hidden with no manage_reply call, and a COVERED nested spam reply under a HIDDEN top-level reply gave action=covered with 0 POSTs. Own replies: process_post (:541-545) skips authors that _protected_author (:561-563) matches against the GET /me username, ignoring case, and run_cycle stops if /me returns no username (:786-789). On the mock, the user's own reply r3 ('提醒：這不是投資建議') got no POST and no CSV row. The script does not request is_reply_owned_by_me. Matching on username is reliable here because the docs say username works for 'your own user'. It also never auto-hides UNHUSHED replies; that is a design choice, and the docs do not define UNHUSHED.

expectations.text: Paginates reply lists with paging.cursors.after rather than reading only the first page.
expectations.evidence: ThreadsClient.get_paged (:252-277) follows paging.next when present. Otherwise it requests the same path again with after=paging.cursors.after. The mock returned cursor-only paging, the same shape as the doc examples (no next). On a post with 60 replies and page size 25, the script made 4 requests (after=MjU=, NTA=, NjA=) and hid the 55th reply ('帶你投資'), so pagination is real. Caveat: with cursor-only paging it requests the next page only when the current page had at least 10 items (CURSOR_PROBE_MIN_ITEMS :86, :272). With a short page that was not the last one (8 of 25, as if some replies were filtered out) or a server page size of 5, it stopped after page 1 and missed the spam (it saw 8 of 30 and 5 of 12 replies). When paging.next was present it read all 30. The executor's cursor-only test uses page_size=10, exactly at the threshold, so this gap is never tested.

expectations.text: States the permissions needed: threads_read_replies and threads_manage_replies (plus threads_basic).

This matches Retrieve and Manage Replies.md: threads_basic for all calls, threads_read_replies for GET reply endpoints, threads_manage_replies for POST.

expectations.text: Writes a CSV log with at least the reply ID, matched keyword or text, action taken and timestamp, and avoids re-processing the same reply on later runs.
expectations.evidence: CsvLog writes threads_moderation_log.csv as UTF-8 with a BOM (bytes start b'\xef\xbb\xbf'). Its columns (CSV_FIELDS :457-461) are checked_at, action, matched_keywords, username, reply_text, depth, reply_id, reply_permalink, reply_time, post_id, post_permalink, target_id, target_permalink, detail. threads_guard_state.json prevents re-processing: Guard._finish stores state.handled[reply_id], and process_post skips IDs found in handled or exempt_ids (:542). On the mock, rows looked like {checked_at: 2026-10-14T10:08:23+08:00, action: hidden, matched_keywords: 加賴, reply_id: r1}, and a second cycle added 0 CSV rows and sent 0 POSTs. test_next_cycles_do_not_repeat_work passes. Minor points: failed hides are retried up to 3 times on purpose, and running '--once --dry-run' from cron writes the same dry_run rows again each time, because dry_seen is kept only in memory.

notes: No user_notes.md was written. These caveats come from response.md: the script was tested only against a simulated API, and field names and error formats are based on the executor's own knowledge of the spec.
The executor says it could not check the latest docs, so it did not hard-code the nested-reply limitation. This is why the script tries the nested ID first.
'投資' is likely to hide ordinary comments (false positives).
The user needs to choose NESTED_FALLBACK: hide the whole top-level branch (default) or log_only.
Whether to replace '投資' with narrower phrases, and which accounts to whitelist (EXEMPT_USERNAMES).
Tries the nested reply ID first and falls back to the top-level ancestor. This is a hedge against an API change the docs do not describe.
Cursor-only pagination is followed only when a page has at least 10 items, to save calls on posts with few replies.
If fields are rejected, it falls back to minimal fields and walks /replies one level at a time.
Final skill version: 29/29 checks (100%) vs 25/29 without the skill (85% averaged per eval). Every eval scores at least as well with the skill.

Baseline variance is real: eval 2 without the skill passed 9/9 this round after failing pagination and refresh checks in rounds 1 and 2. With one run per configuration, a single lucky or unlucky run moves the averages a lot.

Remaining baseline misses are knowledge gaps: it still hedges on ghost post + poll and ships a mode that tries the forbidden combination, shows no exact payloads in the reply, omits the 100-follower requirement for profile_lookup, and calls manage_reply on nested replies before falling back.

Graders found a few overstatements in with-skill replies that trace to the skill's wording: a ghost post's link preview restriction presented as stated in the docs (the docs only say text spoilers are the sole supported feature), 'will definitely be rejected' where the docs don't say how the API reacts, and the two profile-discovery endpoints' 1,000-request limits treated as one shared quota.
Speed and cost: with the skill, mean ~706 s vs ~963 s and ~178K vs ~189K tokens.

expectations.text: Identifies that <script> tags inserted via innerHTML never execute, and loads embed.js once, then triggers re-processing of newly inserted embeds with window.instgrm.Embeds.process().
expectations.evidence: First part is met: response.md item 1 says scripts inserted with innerHTML never run and shows the createElement fix. The rest is not. embed.js is not loaded once. threads-embed.js appends a new embed.js <script> in every per-post same-origin iframe, so up to 60 separate instances run. window.instgrm.Embeds.process() appears nowhere in the response or code. Worse, response.md item 2 and the threads-embed.js header comment say embed.js 'only scans at load time; later-inserted blockquotes are not processed'. That ignores process(), which exists to re-scan the page, and the design works around that wrong premise.

expectations.text: Says the page's CSP must allow https://www.threads.com in both script-src (embed.js) and frame-src (the embed iframes).
expectations.evidence: In this design embed.js runs only inside threads-embed.html, and that page ships its own meta CSP: "script-src 'self' https://www.threads.com https://www.threads.net; frame-src https://www.threads.com https://www.threads.net; ...". The nested threads.com /embed/ iframe is created by that child document, so the child's frame-src governs it, not the parent's. The main page correctly needs only frame-src 'self' and connect-src 'self'. response.md item 4 also explains that a CSP allowing only www.threads.net will block both the script and the iframe once they redirect to www.threads.com. Wherever embed.js actually runs, the guidance covers threads.com in both script-src and frame-src. The prose never names both directives in one sentence for the user's own page, but the delivered CSP and explanation are correct.

expectations.text: Attributes 'the first few load, then the rest stall' to rate limiting from loading too many embeds, and paces loading (pagination, lazy-loading near the viewport, or gating a few/one at a time with delays) instead of letting all 60 process at once.
expectations.evidence: Pacing is implemented. threads-wall.js has IntersectionObserver lazy-loading (rootMargin 800px) and MAX_CONCURRENT = 3, though with no delays or backoff. The attribution is wrong, though. response.md item 2 says explicitly '時序問題，這是「偶爾前幾則有出來」的原因' (a timing guess: embed.js loaded elsewhere and processed only the posts already in the DOM). Rate limiting appears only in item 3, as a general extra load concern ('比較容易被 Threads 限流'). It is not given as the cause of the symptom. The expectation requires rate limiting as the cause.

expectations.text: Detects failed embeds by outcome with a timeout (e.g. the blockquote is never replaced or the iframe never gets a height), shows a fallback card linking to the post, and backs off when failures repeat.
expectations.evidence: Timeouts exist: 12 s in threads-embed.js and 20 s in threads-wall.js. A fallback card with an '在 Threads 查看 ↗' link and a manual '重新載入' button exists. Success is not detected by outcome, though. threads-embed.js settles 'rendered' on the Threads iframe's 'load' event, and if any iframe exists at 12 s it settles 'rendered' with reason 'slow-load'. Real embed.js inserts the /embed/ iframe right away at height 0 and removes the blockquote only after the height postMessage. So a rate-limited or broken embed whose page loads but never sends a height is reported as success, the slot is freed, and no fallback card is shown. The 'not-processed' path fires only if embed.js never creates an iframe at all. Nothing backs off on repeated failures: a failure releases the slot and pump() starts the next post immediately.

expectations.text: Implements the weekly deleted-post check with the oEmbed endpoint (graph.threads.net/v1.0/oembed), not by scraping threads.com pages, and runs it outside the visitor's browser (e.g. a scheduled GitHub Actions job or script).
expectations.evidence: It runs outside the browser: .github/workflows/threads-weekly-check.yml uses cron '17 1 * * 1' and runs node scripts/threads-posts.mjs check. But the check scrapes threads.com. fetchSignals() GETs the post page (or `${post.url}/embed`) with a browser User-Agent, parses <title> and og: meta tags, and compares a fingerprint with responses for randomly made-up post codes. graph.threads.net and oEmbed are never used anywhere.

expectations.text: Correctly states that the oEmbed endpoint can be called without an access token (changelog 2026-03-03), so no app, token or app secret is needed for the check — and never puts an app secret in browser code.
expectations.evidence: The response never mentions oEmbed or the 2026-03-03 change that made it tokenless. It says only that its page-scraping method needs no login or token. In '想跟你確認' item 1 it says an accurate check needs the official API with a Meta developer app and a token renewed about every 60 days, and limits that to the user's own posts. That misses the tokenless oEmbed route for any public post. No app secret is put in browser code, but the main claim is absent.

expectations.text: Removes a post only on the definitive not-found error (code 24 / 'Media Not Found', is_transient false); other errors (5xx, rate limits, network failures, invalid-parameter errors) are treated as transient and never remove posts.
expectations.evidence: classify() in scripts/threads-posts.mjs marks a post 'gone' on HTTP 404/410 from the scraped page, or when its fingerprint (status, final URL path, title, og:title) matches the response for a made-up URL. After 2 consecutive weekly 'gone' results the post is removed. 429, 5xx and timeouts are treated as 'unknown', and there is a 20% mass-removal abort. But removal never depends on oEmbed error code 24 / 'Media Not Found' / is_transient=false. It depends on a heuristic over scraped HTML, which can mark a post gone because of login walls or other generic pages.

expectations.text: Does not put a post's permalink page itself in an iframe (Threads post pages refuse framing); any direct iframe uses the /embed/ URL.
expectations.evidence: The only iframe the code creates directly is the same-origin threads-embed.html?u=..&c=.. (threads-wall.js createCard/start). Inside it, the Threads iframe is created by embed.js from the blockquote, which uses <permalink>/embed/. No code sets an iframe src to a threads.com post permalink. The checker fetches pages with fetch(); it does not frame them.

notes: Executor says it never tested against real Threads; whether real embed.js needs other origins, and whether Threads responses to deleted posts can be told apart from GitHub runners, are unknown.
The 'first few appear' explanation is labeled as an inference from symptoms, without seeing the user's code.
The weekly check scrapes threads.com pages with a browser User-Agent; it should use the tokenless oEmbed endpoint and its code-24 'Media Not Found' signal.
Success detection in threads-embed.js (iframe load event or iframe existing) does not match how real embed.js signals a rendered post (height postMessage, then blockquote removal).
Wraps each post in its own same-origin iframe that loads its own copy of embed.js, instead of loading embed.js once and calling window.instgrm.Embeds.process().

Round 4 adds §11 (embedding posts) to the skill and a new eval 6: a 60-post Threads wall that only shows 'View on Threads' links, plus a weekly check for deleted posts. Only eval 6 was run; the rest of the skill is unchanged from round 3.

With the skill: 8/8. It explained that scripts inserted via innerHTML never run and re-triggered embed.js with window.instgrm.Embeds.process(), named the CSP directives, paced loading to avoid rate limits, detected failures by outcome with fallback cards and backoff, and checked deletions with token-less oEmbed, removing a post only on code 24.

Without the skill: 2/8. It diagnosed the innerHTML problem but believed embed.js only scans the page once, so it wrapped every post in its own iframe page; it treated the iframe load event as success; and it built the deletion check by scraping threads.com pages because it thought an accurate check needed a Meta app and token (oEmbed has worked without a token since 2026-03-03).

Facts not in the docs were checked live on 2026-10-14 and given to the graders as ground truth: embed.js exposes instgrm.Embeds.process(), loads at most 3 embeds at a time and removes each blockquote once its iframe reports a height; post pages send X-Frame-Options: DENY while /embed/ pages can be framed; oEmbed works without a token and returns code 24 (subcode 4279056) for missing posts.

Grader feedback folded into the skill: build the embed markup from a validated URL instead of injecting stored HTML (XSS), and note that old threads.net links produce threads.net iframes, so rewrite them or allow both hosts in the CSP. Graders also flagged assertion 8 (no iframe of the permalink page) as non-discriminating.
Speed and cost: with the skill 964 s and ~193K tokens vs 1,367 s and ~184K without. One run per configuration, so treat the gap as directional.

expectations.text: Returns 200 quickly and does the database work asynchronously (background task/queue), and tolerates duplicate deliveries (idempotent insert keyed on the event/media ID).
expectations.evidence: Graded to the round-5 standard for this assertion: storing the raw event in the request and acknowledging with 200 once it is committed, while the slow work (the Graph API post lookup and status updates) runs as a background task, counts as returning 200 quickly with the database work done asynchronously. Duplicate deliveries are tolerated with a unique key on the event and media ID. Original grader notes: Idempotency is met: db.py:24 has UniqueConstraint('field','media_id') and save_event returns None on IntegrityError (db.py:84-88); in the stub run a redelivery returned 200 and queued 0 background tasks. But the database write is not asynchronous. webhook.py:40-46 awaits save_event (INSERT + COMMIT) inside the request handler before returning 200, and only the Graph API lookup and status updates go to BackgroundTasks (webhook.py:45, 49-60). The response says so: '每個事件先寫進 threads_webhook_events（狀態 pending）再回 200。DB 掛掉就回 500'. Persist-then-ack is a defensible design, but it contradicts 'does the database work asynchronously (background task/queue)', and the assertion has to carry the burden of proof.

Mock run with a flat replies payload: wrong-secret signature -> 403 with 0 rows in threads_webhook_deliveries; missing header -> 403; signature of the compact body sent with re-indented bytes -> 403; valid signature -> 200.

expectations.text: Parses the flat Threads webhook payload (top-level app_id/topic/target_id/time and values.field / values.value), not the entry[].changes[] shape used by other Meta webhooks.

expectations.text: Returns 200 quickly and does the database work asynchronously (background task/queue), and tolerates duplicate deliveries (idempotent insert keyed on the event/media ID).
expectations.evidence: Graded to the round-5 standard for this assertion: storing the raw event in the request and acknowledging with 200 once it is committed, while the slow work (the Graph API post lookup and status updates) runs as a background task, counts as returning 200 quickly with the database work done asynchronously. notes: Round 5 adds four new evals (7–10): a FastAPI webhook endpoint for replies and mentions, Express OAuth login with token refresh, a review of a buggy Python posting script, and posting a long text with emoji for the user as a two-part thread at 8 AM. Only evals 7–10 were run, against skill version 1.1.

With the skill 31/31 checks (100% averaged per eval) vs 27/31 without (87%). The gap is smaller than in rounds 1-4 because this round the baseline could web-search the official docs, and it did look up the webhooks and OAuth pages.
No mock API server this round: executors checked their own code with local mocks or FastAPI's TestClient, and graders judged by reading the code.

Baseline misses: eval 8 never mentions the 90-day permission grant, that private profiles must re-authorize every 90 days, or data_access_expires_at; eval 9 lowercases reply_control without explaining that the UPPER_CASE form is only what reply_audience returns when reading, leaves fbtrace_id out of its errors, and sends the token as a URL query parameter so raise_for_status() can leak it into exceptions; eval 10 only summarises the two parts, lists no parameters and tells the user to start posting without asking for confirmation.

Graders flagged eval 10 assertions 1–5 and 7 (emoji byte counting, verbatim split, reply_to_id chaining, no native scheduling, token check, account check) as non-discriminating: they passed in both configurations, and only assertion 6 (full content and parameters in the reply plus explicit confirmation) told them apart. In eval 7 both configurations write the raw event synchronously in the request and only defer the Graph lookup to a background task.
Speed and cost: with the skill mean ~226 s vs ~282 s and ~121K vs ~104K tokens; the extra ~17K tokens are mostly from reading SKILL.md. One run per configuration, so treat the gap as directional.

expectations.text: Token refresh calls GET https://graph.threads.net/refresh_access_token with grant_type=th_refresh_token and the current long-lived token.
expectations.evidence: threadsToken.ts:295-299 calls `this.options.http.rootGet("refresh_access_token", { grant_type: "th_refresh_token" }, token.accessToken)`; threadsHttp.ts:135-137 builds `{baseUrl}/refresh_access_token` (unversioned) and threadsHttp.ts:148 adds `access_token`. The base URL comes from THREADS_GRAPH_BASE_URL, documented as `https://graph.threads.net` (response.md:38). Grader probe against a local mock: the request hit `/refresh_access_token` with params {grant_type: th_refresh_token, access_token: OLDTOKEN} (the stored token).

expectations.text: Refresh logic follows the documented rules: only refreshes a token that is unexpired and at least 24 h old, refreshes well before the ~60-day expiry, and persists the new token together with its expiry.
expectations.evidence: threadsToken.ts:247-252 rejects an expired stored token before any refresh; :255 refreshes only when fewer than THREADS_TOKEN_REFRESH_DAYS_BEFORE_EXPIRY days remain (15 in response.md:42); :268-271 skips when `issuedAt` is under 24 h old; :304-315 saves the new token with `expiresAt` from `expires_in` right away, then corrects it from debug_token (:328-340). Grader probes (MemStore, mock): expiresAt = now - 1 day -> 0 refresh calls, ThreadsReauthRequiredError; 1 h and 12 h old with 10 days left -> 0 calls; 3 days old with 10 days left -> 1 call, store now holds NEWTOKEN1 with expiry +60 d; 57 days left -> no call. Caveat: when `issuedAt` is null (debug_token gave no issued_at) the 24 h guard is skipped (probe refreshed immediately); age is genuinely unknown there, so per the earlier decision this is a caveat, not a failure.

expectations.text: The reply explains that an already-expired token cannot be refreshed and needs re-authorization, and the code fails loudly / alerts in that case.

expectations.text: The code is TypeScript and does not hard-code the token or the app secret.
expectations.evidence: All five deliverables are .ts. Grader ran TypeScript 5.6.3 `tsc` with `strict: true` on outputs/*.ts in both CommonJS/node10 and ESNext/bundler setups: exit 0 (listFilesOnly confirmed all 5 files checked). The token comes from the TokenStore (threadsToken.ts:238), seeded from THREADS_SEED_ACCESS_TOKEN (seedThreadsToken.ts:19); the app ID/secret come from THREADS_APP_ID/THREADS_APP_SECRET via requireEnv (dailyThreadsJob.ts:85-86). No literal token or secret appears in the code.

notes: debug_token: the code calls `GET /v1.0/debug_token` with the app token `TH|<APP_ID>|<APP_SECRET>` as access_token and the user token as input_token (threadsToken.ts:214-219; grader probe recorded access_token=TH|APPID|APPSECRET). Nothing depends on the account being a Threads tester: seed checks is_valid, expires_at, short-lived lifetime and scopes, refresh re-reads expiry, and checkDataAccess (:353-381) warns about `data_access_expires_at` and escalates to critical once it has passed. The round 1-3 limitation (90-day grant check skipped for non-testers) is gone in this run.
The 90-day grant check is skipped silently when `dataAccessExpiresAt` is null, i.e. when debug_token returned no data_access_expires_at (threadsToken.ts:356); no notice is raised in that case.

The 24 h guard relies on debug_token's `issued_at`; when it is missing (`issuedAt: null`) the token is refreshed as soon as it enters the window. The docs list issued_at in the debug_token response, so this is an edge case (recorded as a caveat under assertion 2).

follower_demographics handling matches the docs' warning that the breakdown shape is undocumented: it logs the raw JSON at debug level and accepts three shapes, raising an error with the raw JSON when none match (threadsInsights.ts:251-258, 328-357). The reply also correctly says post insights are lifetime totals, not daily deltas (response.md:67).

expectations.text: Handles the GET verification request: returns hub.challenge (as plain text) only when hub.verify_token matches the configured token, otherwise 403.

expectations.text: Verifies every POST with the X-Hub-Signature-256 header: HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body keyed with the app secret, compared in constant time, rejecting mismatches.
expectations.evidence: threads_webhook.py:318-321 reads raw = await request.body() before parsing and calls signature_is_valid (137-142): hmac.new(secret, raw, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest() compared with hmac.compare_digest against the 'sha256=' header value; a mismatch returns 403. Grader probe: unsigned, wrong-secret and tampered-body POSTs all got 403 and wrote 0 rows.

expectations.text: Refresh logic follows the documented rules: only refreshes a token that is unexpired and at least 24 h old, refreshes well before the ~60-day expiry, and persists the new token together with its expiry.

Grader probes: expiresAt = now - 1 day -> TokenExpiredError, 0 refresh calls; 1 h and 12 h old with 10 days left -> 0 calls; 3 days old -> 1 call, store holds NEWTOKEN1 with expiry +60 d; 57 days left -> no call. Caveat: the manual `seedToken.ts refresh` path (forceRefresh, :244-249) skips the age check, and a probe sent a 1 h-old token to the endpoint. That path is an operator override whose comment defers to the API's 24 h rule, so the scheduled logic is judged compliant.

expectations.text: The code is TypeScript and does not hard-code the token or the app secret.
expectations.evidence: All deliverables are .ts. Grader ran TypeScript 5.6.3 `tsc` with `strict: true`, NodeNext, @types/node on outputs/*.ts: exit 0 (listFilesOnly confirmed all 7 files checked). The token is read from the TokenStore (FileTokenStore at THREADS_TOKEN_STORE_PATH, config.ts:124-126) or from argv/stdin in seedToken.ts; the app secret comes from THREADS_APP_SECRET (config.ts:136-146). notes: debug_token: this run never calls `GET /debug_token` (only `input_token` appears, in a redaction list, threadsClient.ts:11), so it doesn't use the app token, a tester's token or the account's own token. Token expiry is known only from `expires_in` at save time. The 90-day permission grant (`data_access_expires_at`) isn't tracked at all, for any account, and the reply never mentions it, so a private profile's grant would lapse with no warning. The round 1-3 limitation is still there, in a wider form: the check is missing entirely.

Operator paths ignore the 24 h rule even when the age is known: `seedToken.ts refresh` (forceRefresh, tokenManager.ts:244-249) sent a 1 h-old token to /refresh_access_token in a grader probe. `seedToken.ts long` refreshes a pasted token of unknown age immediately (seedToken.ts:75-79). The API would just reject these calls, but the code's comment claims the rule is still applied.

If saving the refreshed token fails, refreshAndSave logs an error and throws. resolveToken then treats that as a transient failure, logs a warning and returns the old token (tokenManager.ts:267-277, 289-297), so the new token is discarded.

fetchFollowerCountries assumes `total_value.breakdowns[].dimension_keys` contains "country". If that key is missing it returns an empty list as a success (threadsInsights.ts:265-269), with no raw-JSON log, even though the docs don't show the breakdown shape, so a shape mismatch would silently write no country data.

expectations.text: Is honest that refreshing does not cover everyone: permission grants last 90 days, and private profiles must re-authorize every 90 days even though their tokens refresh; suggests tracking data_access_expires_at (debug_token) and prompting re-authorization.
expectations.evidence: Neither the reply nor the code mentions the 90-day permission grant, private profiles, data_access_expires_at or debug_token (grader grep of outputs/ finds none). response.md line 56 says the opposite: 「只要在過期前持續續期，用戶就永遠不用重登」. Line 57 lists only three unrecoverable cases: app removed, token invalidated (190), or the scheduler stopped for more than 60 days. expectations.text: Keeps the app secret and tokens server-side (env/secret store, never in front-end code or logs).
expectations.evidence: THREADS_APP_SECRET is read from env only (config.js:57). Tokens are stored AES-256-GCM encrypted, bound to threads_user_id (tokenCipher.js). The session cookie holds only the signed account ID (session.js), and /api/me returns status and expiry but no token (authRoutes.js:138-145). notes: debug_token: not used anywhere, so no access_token choice applies. The run never reads data_access_expires_at, so it does no 90-day tracking for any user, testers or not.

Error parsing bug: threadsClient.js:86-96 only reads the {error:{message}} envelope. The documented code-exchange error is the flat {error_type, code, error_message} shape. Grader probe: a flat 'Matching code was not found or was already used' (and a flat redirect_uri error) both ended as reason=threads_api_error, logged as 「HTTP 400（非 JSON 回應）」. So the code_used_or_expired / redirect_uri_mismatch classification (authRoutes.js:24-32) never fires for the user's two errors, and the log hides the real message. The run's own mock used the nested envelope, so its tests missed this.

Implements the deauthorize and data-deletion callbacks, verifying signed_request with HMAC-SHA256 against the Threads app secret (metaCallbacks.js), which the with_skill run left out. The refresh worker runs inside the web process via setInterval, with DB leases to avoid double refreshes.

Round 6 reruns evals 2, 4, 7 and 8 against skill version 1.3 to check two changes that hadn't been evaluated: the §10 (practice) line on idempotent webhook processing and the §8.4 debug_token update (since the 2026-08-18 changelog, access_token may be the app token TH|<APP_ID>|<APP_SECRET>, not only a Threads tester's token). Neither configuration had web access: the baseline relied on the model alone, as in rounds 1–4, so evals 7 and 8 can't be compared directly with round 5, where the baseline searched the official docs.
With the skill 31/31 checks (100%) vs 26/31 without (84% averaged per eval). Every eval scores higher with the skill, and no with-skill score dropped compared with earlier rounds.

Webhook deduplication: the with-skill eval 7 run keys deliveries on UNIQUE(field, media_id) with media_id = values.value.id. Grader probes: a redelivery that differs only in time is stored once, and a replies event and a mentions event for the same media ID are kept as two rows.

debug_token: the with-skill runs of evals 2 and 8 call debug_token with the app token, so the 90-day grant check (data_access_expires_at) works for every account, not only Threads testers; the eval 2 limitation noted in rounds 1–3 is gone. The with-skill eval 4 reply still calls debug_token with the user's own token, says the token owner must be a Threads tester and never mentions the app token, so the change didn't reach that answer. No assertion covers this.

Baseline misses: eval 2 reads paging.cursors.after only when paging.next exists (the round 1–2 bug); eval 4 never states the 100-follower threshold (as in rounds 2–3); eval 7 says target_id is always the brand's user ID, so in a grader probe every docs-shaped replies event was marked ignored and dropped, and it never mentions business verification; eval 8 never mentions the 90-day permission grant (as in round 5), and its client reads only the nested error envelope, so the flat code-exchange errors the user reported surface as a generic error.

Graders flagged most assertions as non-discriminating this round: only assertion 8 separated eval 2, 4 separated eval 4, 4 and 6 separated eval 7, and 7 separated eval 8. They suggested scoring 90-day grant tracking (eval 2), the debug_token app-token option (eval 4), that a docs-shaped replies event is actually stored (eval 7), and parsing the flat code-exchange error (eval 8).

Process: the eval 2 baseline and both eval 8 runs were stopped partway at the user's request and rerun from scratch with the same instructions on 2026-10-19 around 11:26 UTC; the partial outputs were discarded. No mock server: executors tested against their own local mocks, and graders re-ran those tests and probed behaviour with mocks of their own. Speed and cost: with the skill mean ~1,117 s and ~211K tokens vs ~1,000 s and ~170K without. One run per configuration, so treat the gap as directional.

notes: Reference client: the run read scripts/threads_client.py at transcript line 23 (12:25:20Z), right after SKILL.md and about five minutes before writing threads_carousel.py (12:30:40Z). process_log.md:5 says it ported call()/check()/wait_ready()/publish(). This is build mode with no posting requested, so the operate-mode steps (run the client from work/, check before publish) don't apply.

Port fidelity: call() became ThreadsClient.call (requests instead of urllib, same encoding rules, ThreadsError parsing both error shapes, plus a transient flag, a code-190 hint and a network error that drops the token-bearing URL). check() became validate_carousel (2-20 items, IMAGE/VIDEO per item, alt_text <= 1,000, the same emoji-byte text_len and URL regex, <= 5 links, topic-tag rules, plus a reply_control enum check). It left out the TEXT_ONLY/poll/ghost checks, which is reasonable since this function can't send those fields.

wait_ready() became wait_until_finished, which polls all items together with the same fields and the same ERROR/EXPIRED/PUBLISHED stops. Two deliberate changes: a timeout returns the pending set (for --resume) instead of raising, and transient poll errors are tolerated. publish() is kept end to end, including the permalink-only lookup that doesn't fail a live post (probe: exit 0 with "已發布（media ID media-1），但沒有取得貼文網址"). Nothing was ported wrongly.

Quota and waiting: it checks threads_publishing_limit (quota_usage,config) before creating containers and stops when usage >= quota_total; any error from that call aborts before a container exists. Polling starts immediately, then waits 5 s doubling to 60 s, with up to 600 s per stage (JSON config). It also re-checks status on a publish with no media ID and republishes the same container. Beyond the requested function it ships a CLI with a JSON config and --resume, which SKILL.md §2 step 4 cautions against; the grader reran work/test_carousel.py from a scratch copy and got 13/13.

Reference client port: threadsHttp.ts keeps call()'s behaviours: one helper adds the token, parses both error envelopes (nested `error` and the flat error_type/error_message shape, :131-137), and raises a typed error with code/type/message/fbtrace_id. The round 1-3 limitation is gone; the grant check is skipped only when the debug_token call itself errors (warning, :187-197).

The reply correctly explains the 90-day data-access grant (public profiles are extended by refresh; private ones must re-authorize every 90 days), says the views metrics are lifetime totals rather than daily increments, and says follower_demographics' breakdown shape is undocumented, so it parses defensively with a raw-JSON fallback. notes: Quota and waiting: it never checks threads_publishing_limit. Polling uses a fixed interval (THREADS_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS, 30 s in the example) and a per-stage timeout (THREADS_PROCESSING_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, 900 s), both from env with no defaults. On timeout it keeps the containers and prints --resume-children; a failed publish is not resent blindly: it checks status first (PUBLISHED stops, FINISHED resends).

Post-publish lookup asks for fields=id,permalink (threads_carousel.py:311). `id` needs no extra permission, and a failed lookup is caught: the grader probe got exit 0 and "貼文已發布（media id media-1），但暫時拿不到網址…", so a good post isn't reported as a failure.

Validation is shallower than the docs: text length uses len(text), with no emoji UTF-8 byte counting (SKILL.md §4.4), there is no 5-link limit check, and alt_text isn't supported. Container-creation POSTs are retried on transient errors, which can leave a stray unpublished container (harmless, as its own comment notes). Error parsing handles only the {"error": {...}} envelope.

response.md says the in-caption URL "會是可點的連結". The docs snapshot only says it stays plain text with no preview card, so that's unverified rather than shown wrong. The reply honestly says the parameter names and limits came from memory. The grader reran work/test_threads_carousel.py from a scratch copy: 21 passed.

expectations.text: Token refresh calls GET https://graph.threads.net/refresh_access_token with grant_type=th_refresh_token and the current long-lived token.
