expectations.text: Refresh logic follows the documented rules: only refreshes a token that is unexpired and at least 24 h old, refreshes well before the ~60-day expiry, and persists the new token together with its expiry.
expectations.evidence: threads-token.ts:199-203 throws ThreadsTokenExpiredError when expiresAt has passed; :205-210 returns 'valid' or 'too-new-to-refresh' unless days left <= THREADS_TOKEN_REFRESH_WHEN_DAYS_LEFT (recommended 30, threads.env.example:12) and age >= 24 h; :225 saves {accessToken, expiresAt, issuedAt} atomically (:84-89). Grader probe (threshold 30 d): expired -> throw, 0 calls; 1 h / 12 h old -> too-new-to-refresh, 0 calls; 3 d old -> 1 call, NEW token saved with expiresAt now+60 d; 50 d left -> no call. Caveat (per earlier rounds, not a failure): the one-off bootstrap `import` mode (threads-token-bootstrap.ts:36-44) refreshes an env-supplied token of unknown age immediately; its comment says a token under 24 h will be rejected.

expectations.text: The reply explains that an already-expired token cannot be refreshed and needs re-authorization, and the code fails loudly / alerts in that case.

expectations.text: Yesterday's posts are listed via GET /me/threads (or /{user-id}/threads) using since/until or timestamp filtering, with cursor pagination via paging.cursors.after and limit <= 100.
expectations.evidence: Pagination only follows paging.next: threads-insights.ts:219-222 breaks when `page.paging?.next` is undefined and never builds an after=<paging.cursors.after> request. The docs say list responses carry only paging.cursors and no next URL (SKILL.md §5); this is the pattern earlier rounds failed. Grader probe with documented-shape pages (cursors only): only 1 request was made and 2 of 4 posts were returned. limit is also not capped: THREADS_PAGE_SIZE only has a minimum of 1 (threads-config.ts:108; example value 50). since/until plus timestamp filtering on /me/threads are fine (:197-208).

expectations.text: The code is TypeScript and does not hard-code the token or the app secret.
expectations.evidence: All deliverables are .ts. Grader ran tsc 5.6.3 --strict (NodeNext, @types/node 22) on a copy of the source files (test excluded): exit 0. The token comes from the token file, and THREADS_SHORT_LIVED_TOKEN / THREADS_LONG_LIVED_TOKEN / THREADS_APP_SECRET come from env only in the bootstrap CLI (threads-token-bootstrap.ts:28-39). There are no literals.

notes: debug_token: never used, by the code or the reply. Nothing checks the token's validity beyond the locally stored expiresAt, its scopes, or the 90-day data-access grant (data_access_expires_at). The reply never mentions the 90-day grant, so private-profile accounts would still break every 90 days with no warning, though no assertion scores this.

Error parsing only recognises the nested {error:{...}} envelope (threads-http.ts:98-102). A flat error_type/code/error_message body (the only shape the docs show, for token endpoints) gets code=null, so a 190 from refresh in that shape would be logged as a transient 'refresh-failed' rather than ThreadsTokenExpiredError. The next Graph call's 190 would still abort the job.

The reply states as fact that follower_demographics values sit in total_value.breakdowns[0].results[] with dimension_values, and the code throws if the shape differs, without logging the raw JSON. The docs don't show this structure (SKILL.md §7), so it is an unverified assumption, likely carried over from Instagram insights.

The run shipped a one-off bootstrap CLI and a 23 KB test file in outputs/ beyond the two requested modules. Its mock encoded its own assumptions (paging.next, /{id}/threads_insights), so the 21 passing tests didn't catch either failing assertion.

expectations.text: The reply itself (not only a script) shows the exact payload for each alternative, keeping the user's text verbatim, with poll_attachment {option_a: 淺焙, option_b: 深焙} on a TEXT post for the poll option and is_ghost_post=true for the ghost option.

It has no `media_type=TEXT` and no `poll_attachment={"option_a":"淺焙","option_b":"深焙"}` for A. `is_ghost_post=true` appears only in the conflict explanation (line 5), not as B's payload. The user's text is verbatim in the commands, but that doesn't make up for the missing payload.

expectations.text: It plans to verify which account it will post to (e.g. GET /me?fields=id,username) before publishing.
expectations.evidence: response.md:24 says the script defaults to a dry-run that only checks which account the token belongs to and prints the content. Its dry-run calls `GET me?fields=id,username` and prints "token 對應帳號：@…" (threads_post.py:227-228). Lines 44-48 lay out A as "先 dry-run，確認帳號和內容" and then "確認沒問題，就加上 --publish". Caveat: B's command (line 51) goes straight to `--publish`. A grader probe against the run's mock showed it prints the account, then creates and publishes with no pause (GET /me → POST threads → GET status → POST threads_publish). It passed because the stated plan puts the account check before publishing and the user must pick an option first, but B's path on its own matches the pattern that failed in round 1.

expectations.text: Beyond the API conflict, it flags at least one way the request as written could undercut the user's goal — e.g. a 24-hour post published now (midweek) is gone before the weekend it advertises, or the link looks like a placeholder.
expectations.evidence: response.md:16 "「週末限定」通常橫跨六、日兩天，限時貼文如果週六發，週日活動還沒結束就消失了": a 24 h ghost post can't cover the weekend promo. Line 18 also flags that the poll question isn't in the text. It doesn't flag that posting now (Monday 10/19) means the post is gone before the weekend starts, or that example.com is a placeholder.

notes: No skill. The run wrote its own stdlib CLI (outputs/threads_post.py): dry-run by default, a local ghost+poll block, container → status → publish → permalink, and no blind retry after a publish timeout. It ran 13 unittest tests against a FastAPI mock, and all passed (transcript event 58).

Missed hazards: it treats "直接幫我發" as if the post would go out on Saturday and never flags that publishing now (Monday) kills the weekend promo. It doesn't flag the example.com placeholder link or show a counted length.

Unsupported claim: "投票本身 24 小時後就會自動截止" (response.md:6, repeated in the script's error message). The docs snapshot says there's no poll-duration parameter and to read `expiration_timestamp`; it doesn't state a 24 h duration. The run builds on this to guess that the user confused the poll's close with the ghost post, and it recommends option A.

The script's 500-char check uses len(text) (threads_post.py:64) rather than the documented UTF-8 byte count for emoji. In a grader probe, 249 ☕️ (1,494 under the docs' rule) passed the local check. This is harmless for this 54-count text. The handover gives `$env:THREADS_API_BASE` (required, with no default) but no token-setup line.

SKILL.md §5 says the docs' list responses carry `paging.cursors.before/after` and no `next` URLs, so on the documented shape this reads only page 1. Grader probe with cursors-only pages: P1/conversation was requested once (no `after`), and the top-level spam "加賴賺錢" (R4) and nested "私訊我" (R4a) on page 2 were never hidden or logged. With `paging.next` added to the same mock, R4 was hidden, confirming the loop depends on `next`.

expectations.text: States the permissions needed: threads_read_replies and threads_manage_replies (plus threads_basic).
expectations.evidence: response.md "使用前準備" step 1: "你的 Meta App 要有 `threads_basic`、`threads_read_replies`、`threads_manage_replies` 三個權限"; also the script docstring (threads_reply_guard.py:7).

expectations.text: Writes a CSV log with at least the reply ID, matched keyword or text, action taken and timestamp, and avoids re-processing the same reply on later runs.
expectations.evidence: CSV columns include logged_at, action, reply_id, matched_keywords, note and reply_text (threads_reply_guard.py:84-99). Already-hidden replies are skipped on later runs via the API's hide_status (server-side state that survives a restart), and record-only actions are de-duplicated by (mode, reply_id, action) read back from the CSV on startup (:390-404, :607-610). Grader probe: a second `--once` run made no new manage_reply calls and added no rows. Caveat (as in round 2): a hide that keeps failing is retried every cycle and gets a new `failed` row each time (probe: two R5 `failed` rows after two runs).

notes: The stricter Assertion 5 reading changed this verdict: under rounds 2–3, a loop that paginated only while `paging.next` was present passed with a caveat, so this `next`-only loop would likely have passed then; under this round's documented-shape standard it fails (probe: page-2 spam missed).

Nested policy default is `hide_top_level` (config.example.json:6): out of the box a spam nested reply makes the script hide its top-level ancestor and the whole branch (probe: R1, an innocent "你好", hidden for nested R1a), and response.md warns about the collateral hiding and suggests a `--dry-run` first. This handles nested spam as the user asked, but because of the pagination bug it would only cover the first page of each post's conversation on the real API.

Re-processing is avoided mostly through the API's hide_status rather than a local list, which held up across restarts in the probe; failed hides are retried every cycle with a fresh `failed` row (the round 2 caveat), and HTTP 429/5xx/rate-limit codes are retried in-process with exponential backoff (max_retries in config).

response.md's last paragraph suggests removing `is_reply_owned_by_me` from REPLY_FIELDS if the API rejects it, though SKILL.md §6 documents that field; harmless because the script also matches the username. The run did not read the skill (process_log.md:4; no skill-snapshot or threads_client references in its transcript).

Loading is paced (IntersectionObserver plus concurrency 3), but round 4 requires the rate-limit attribution, so this fails.

expectations.text: Detects failed embeds by outcome with a timeout (e.g. the blockquote is never replaced or the iframe never gets a height), shows a fallback card linking to the post, and backs off when failures repeat.
expectations.evidence: Success is the inner Threads iframe's load event. buildFrameContent sets 'ready' when that iframe fires load with an http(s) src (threads-wall.js:148-161). Round 4 failed this pattern: embed.js inserts the iframe at height 0, and a rate-limited or error page fires load too, so such a post shows as 'ready' with the bare link box. The 15 s timeout gives a 'fallback' only if no inner iframe exists yet (:199); otherwise the card goes to 'timeout' and the frame is left loading. Nothing backs off after repeated failures: createLoadQueue (threads-lib.js:61-94) just hands the slot to the next post.

expectations.text: Implements the weekly deleted-post check with the oEmbed endpoint (graph.threads.net/v1.0/oembed), not by scraping threads.com pages, and runs it outside the visitor's browser (e.g. a scheduled GitHub Actions job or script).
expectations.evidence: prune-deleted-posts.mjs:98-122 calls THREADS_OEMBED_ENDPOINT with ?url=..., and prune-threads-posts.yml:39 sets it to https://graph.threads.net/v1.0/oembed. No threads.com pages are fetched. The check runs in GitHub Actions on cron "23 1 * * 1" plus workflow_dispatch (yml:3-12), outside the browser.

expectations.text: Correctly states that the oEmbed endpoint can be called without an access token (changelog 2026-03-03), so no app, token or app secret is needed for the check — and never puts an app secret in browser code.
expectations.evidence: The reply never says the endpoint works without a token. It says "我在這裡沒辦法連到 Meta 確認這個端點要不要 token" (response.md:78), and if a token error comes back it tells the user to create a token with their Threads App, even mentioning renewing a 60-day long-lived user token. The token is optional and stays server-side, with no secret in browser code. But the required statement that oEmbed needs no token since 2026-03-03 is missing.

expectations.text: Removes a post only on the definitive not-found error (code 24 / 'Media Not Found', is_transient false); other errors (5xx, rate limits, network failures, invalid-parameter errors) are treated as transient and never remove posts.
expectations.evidence: classify() (prune-deleted-posts.mjs:72-96) removes on HTTP 404, or HTTP 400 with code 100 (NOT_FOUND_ERROR_CODES = {100}, :16). code 100 is the invalid-parameter error. The real not-found error, code 24 'Media Not Found', falls through to 'unknown' and is never removed. Grader probe against a local mock: the code-24 post was kept and flagged for manual review. The code 100/2207047 post was removed after its recheck and archived to posts-removed.json. Rate limits abort the run and 5xx/network errors are kept, but the not-found rule is backwards.

expectations.text: Does not put a post's permalink page itself in an iframe (Threads post pages refuse framing); any direct iframe uses the /embed/ URL.
expectations.evidence: The only iframe the code creates directly is a same-origin srcdoc frame (threads-wall.js:176-215). The Threads iframe inside it comes from embed.js, which uses the /embed/ URL. No permalink page is framed.

notes: XSS: the wall never injects the stored embed code. It builds the blockquote inside each srcdoc frame with DOM methods, from a URL that parseThreadsUrl checks (threads.com/threads.net hosts, /@user/post/CODE path). The one-off migrate-posts.mjs pulls data-text-post-permalink out of the stored embed code with a regex and keeps only URLs.

threads.net links: the front end, the migration script and the prune script all rewrite them to the configured canonical origin https://www.threads.com. The CSP also allows both hosts. The reply's reason (CSP checks every redirect hop) differs from the documented one (the iframe host follows the permalink), but the result is safe.

The weekly job never removes a truly deleted post. code 24 is classified 'unknown' and flagged for attention, and the workflow fails whenever attention != 0 (prune-threads-posts.yml:60-64). So every week a deleted post stays and the job fails. /t/CODE short links also stay flagged forever, although SKILL §11.1 lists the /t/{shortcode} form as valid for oEmbed.

The srcdoc-per-post wall still starts up to 3 embeds back to back with no gap. Scrolling through 60 posts can hit the embed rate limit, and those posts would be marked 'ready' while showing only the link box. The CSP also adds style-src 'unsafe-inline'.

expectations.text: Handles the GET verification request: returns hub.challenge (as plain text) only when hub.verify_token matches the configured token, otherwise 403.
expectations.evidence: main.py:238-249: verify_callback returns PlainTextResponse(challenge) only when hub.mode == 'subscribe' and hub.verify_token matches (hmac.compare_digest on bytes), otherwise raises HTTPException(403). Grader probe: matching token -> 200 text/plain '1158201444'; wrong token -> 403; mode=unsubscribe -> 403. A request with no hub.verify_token gets 422 (same as with_skill), which was not counted against it.

expectations.text: Verifies every POST with the X-Hub-Signature-256 header: HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body keyed with the app secret, compared in constant time, rejecting mismatches.
expectations.evidence: verify_signature (main.py:60-69) computes HMAC-SHA256 of the raw bytes with the app secret and compares with hmac.compare_digest. receive (251-258) verifies `await request.body()` before json.loads and rejects with 401. Grader probe: no header, wrong secret, and a signature over a re-serialised body all -> 401 with 0 rows stored.

expectations.text: Parses the flat Threads webhook payload (top-level app_id/topic/target_id/time and values.field / values.value), not the entry[].changes[] shape used by other Meta webhooks.
expectations.evidence: parse_event (main.py:76-100) reads top-level app_id/topic/target_id/time and values.field / values.value; the docstring shows the flat shape. Grader probe: docs-shaped replies/mentions processed; an entry[].changes[] body was stored as 'ignored' ('無法辨識的通知格式').

expectations.text: States and implements that target_id is the media ID for `replies` events but the mentioned user's ID for `mentions` events, so mentions are matched to a post via values.value (e.g. its id/root_post/replied_to) rather than target_id.
expectations.evidence: The run states the wrong semantics for replies. response.md:34 says target_id '是被訂閱帳號（也就是你的品牌帳號）的 Threads user id，不是貼文 id' for every event; the docstring (main.py:80), settings.py:24 and env.example:7 say the same. Per the docs, target_id is the media ID for replies. The code reflects the misreading: main.py:192-197 logs a warning ('請確認 token 是否屬於這個帳號') whenever target_id != THREADS_USER_ID, and stores target_id as threads_interactions.account_id. Grader probe: a docs-shaped reply (target_id=5001) triggered that warning and stored account_id='5001'. The event was not dropped, and mentions are correctly matched via values.value.id, but the assertion requires stating the replies semantics, which the run gets wrong.

expectations.text: Returns 200 quickly and does the database work asynchronously (background task/queue), and tolerates duplicate deliveries (idempotent insert keyed on the event/media ID).
expectations.evidence: receive inserts the raw event synchronously (storage.insert_event, ON CONFLICT (dedupe_key) DO NOTHING) and queues process_event via BackgroundTasks before returning (main.py:265-286). That matches the round 5 precedent. Dedup key = '<field>:<values.value.id>' (main.py:103-107, storage.py:17 UNIQUE); a SHA-256 of the raw JSON is used only when field/value.id is missing. Grader probe: the same reply redelivered with only `time` changed -> 1 event row and 1 interaction (second response accepted 0).

expectations.text: Explains that no events arrive because the app is in development mode: webhook delivery needs the app in Live mode (with Advanced Access), plus a verified business.
expectations.evidence: response.md:5-12 names development mode as the cause and says to pass App Review for threads_basic/threads_read_replies/threads_manage_mentions and then switch to Live mode. It never mentions business verification (no '商家驗證'/'business' anywhere in outputs/) or Advanced Access. Round 6 failed a run that omitted business verification.

expectations.text: Names the subscriptions and permissions involved: subscribe to the `replies` and `mentions` fields, with threads_read_replies for replies and threads_manage_mentions for mentions, granted by the account.
expectations.evidence: response.md:11 lists 'threads_read_replies（給 replies 用）、threads_manage_mentions（給 mentions 用）'. response.md:25 says to subscribe `replies` and `mentions` individually. response.md:29 says the brand account's token must include those scopes, re-authorizing if the grant predates the permissions.

expectations.text: Reads the app secret and verify token from the environment/config, never hard-coded, and uses the Threads app secret (not the Facebook app secret).
expectations.evidence: settings.py:11-47 requires every setting (THREADS_APP_SECRET, THREADS_WEBHOOK_VERIFY_TOKEN, …) from the environment with no defaults; a missing or blank one raises SettingsError. Nothing is hard-coded. settings.py:20, env.example:3 and response.md:27 specify the 'Threads App Secret' from the Threads use-case settings page, '不是 App 基本設定頁的那一組'.

notes: Dedup probe: the key is '<values.field>:<values.value.id>' (UNIQUE dedupe_key; a SHA-256 of the sorted raw JSON is used only when field/id are missing). Sending the same reply twice with only `time` changed stored 1 event row and 1 interaction. A `replies` event and a `mentions` event with the same values.value.id (5001) stored 2 event rows and 2 interaction rows (UNIQUE(kind, media_id)); neither was lost.

The target_id misreading has visible side effects: every docs-shaped replies event logs a misleading warning telling the operator to check the token's account, threads_interactions.account_id holds the reply's media ID, and the code requires a THREADS_USER_ID setting built on that premise.

There is no Graph fallback for the parent post. If a replies payload lacks root_post/replied_to, no lookup is made and the row is marked processed with no post info and no error. In a grader probe, a minimal reply payload got root_post_id None and made 0 Graph calls; with_skill resolves the same payload via GET /{reply-id}.

Unverified claims: response.md:7 says dev-mode apps only receive the Dashboard 'Test' sample notifications, and response.md:11-12 makes App Review a prerequisite for going Live. Neither appears in the docs snapshot, which says the docs conflict on App Review. The reply openly says it couldn't check current docs (response.md:3).

expectations.text: Points out that the ID/secret at the top of Basic settings is most likely the Facebook (Meta) app pair, and that the Threads app ID and Threads app secret (listed under the Threads use case settings) must be used instead.
expectations.evidence: response.md:5-11 (heading '用錯了應用程式編號和密鑰（最可能的主因）'): "「應用程式設定 → 基本資料」最上面那組，是 Meta 應用程式本身的編號和密鑰，給 Facebook 登入和 graph.facebook.com 用", and points to "應用程式主控板 → 使用案例 → 存取 Threads API → 自訂 → 設定 →「Threads 應用程式編號」「Threads 應用程式密鑰」" for client_id/client_secret. Repeated in .env.example:12-14 and config.js:13-14.

expectations.text: Builds the authorize URL on threads.com (or threads.net)/oauth/authorize with client_id, redirect_uri, scope including threads_basic and threads_content_publish, response_type=code and a random state that is verified in the callback.
expectations.evidence: threadsClient.js:95-103 sets client_id, redirect_uri, scope, response_type=code and state on THREADS_AUTHORIZE_URL (.env.example:20 'https://threads.net/oauth/authorize'); .env.example:19 sets THREADS_SCOPES=threads_basic,threads_content_publish. threadsAuthRoutes.js:69-71 makes state with randomBytes(32), stores its hash in the DB and sets an HttpOnly cookie; the callback compares it with timingSafeEqual (82-85) and atomically consumes it (99). Grader probe: a callback with no cookie or a forged state redirected to /login?reason=invalid_state with no code exchange.

expectations.text: Explains the 'Matching code was not found or was already used' causes: the code is single-use (e.g. the callback ran twice or the page was refreshed), expires after 1 hour, or a trailing `#_` was left on a copied code.
expectations.evidence: response.md:13-19: "code 只能用一次，而且 1 小時後失效", with causes "使用者在 callback 頁按了重新整理", the SPA and backend both exchanging, React StrictMode running useEffect twice, and "前端從 `location.href` 抓 code，連 Threads 加在網址尾巴的 `#_` 也一起帶走了". threadsAuthRoutes.js:112 strips `#_` (the grader probe confirmed).

expectations.text: Exchanges the code server-side with POST https://graph.threads.net/oauth/access_token (client_id, client_secret, code, grant_type=authorization_code, redirect_uri) and stresses that redirect_uri must match the authorize step and the dashboard entry exactly, including any trailing slash.
expectations.evidence: threadsClient.js:108-122 POSTs form-encoded client_id, client_secret, grant_type=authorization_code, redirect_uri and code to `${graphBaseUrl}/oauth/access_token` (https://graph.threads.net, .env.example:21); the grader probe confirmed. response.md:24: "授權和換 token 這兩步送出的字串要**逐字相同**", listing "結尾多一個 `/`"; response.md:90 and .env.example:17 say the dashboard entry must equal THREADS_REDIRECT_URI "逐字相同（https、網域、www、路徑、結尾斜線）".

expectations.text: Immediately swaps the 1-hour short-lived token for a long-lived one with GET https://graph.threads.net/access_token?grant_type=th_exchange_token, while the short-lived token is still valid.
expectations.evidence: threadsAuthRoutes.js:115-116 exchanges for a long-lived token right after the code exchange; threadsClient.js:125-137 sends GET /access_token with grant_type=th_exchange_token, client_secret and the short-lived token (response.md:47). Confirmed by the grader probe.

expectations.text: Stores each user's token with its expiry (from expires_in) and refreshes it with GET /refresh_access_token?grant_type=th_refresh_token on a schedule, only when it is at least 24 h old and before it expires.
expectations.evidence: threadsAuthRoutes.js:125-132 stores expiresAt from expires_in. tokenRefresher.js:41-85 runs on a setInterval; tokenStore.js:92-115 claims only active rows with token_issued_at <= now - TOKEN_REFRESH_AFTER_DAYS (config.js:78-85 forces at least 1 day) and token_expires_at > now; threadsClient.js:140-151 calls GET /refresh_access_token with grant_type=th_refresh_token. Grader probe: a 23 h-old token was skipped, a 25 h-old one refreshed (TOKEN_REFRESH_AFTER_DAYS=1), an expired one marked needs_reauth with no refresh call.

expectations.text: Is honest that refreshing does not cover everyone: permission grants last 90 days, and private profiles must re-authorize every 90 days even though their tokens refresh; suggests tracking data_access_expires_at (debug_token) and prompting re-authorization.
expectations.evidence: Missing entirely: the response and code never mention the 90-day permission grant, private profiles, data_access_expires_at or debug_token (grep of outputs finds none). Instead response.md:55 says "只要在過期前持續 refresh，使用者就不必重新登入", and response.md:64 lists the only re-login cases as revoked authorization, more than 60 days without refresh, or new scopes. That implies refresh alone keeps every user logged in, the same failure as rounds 5 and 6.

expectations.text: Keeps the app secret and tokens server-side (env/secret store, never in front-end code or logs).
expectations.evidence: App secret and encryption key come only from env (config.js:7-32, no defaults); tokens are stored AES-256-GCM encrypted (tokenCrypto.js) and nulled on revoke; errors carry the endpoint path, not the query string (threadsClient.js:2, 51-66); logs carry user id/username and error fields only. The grader probe found no token or secret in any log entry.

notes: debug_token: never called. Nothing reads data_access_expires_at, so private-profile users whose 90-day grant lapses would appear 'active' until a call fails; /api/threads/account reports only token status.

Error parsing gap: threadsClient.js:79-88 reads only the {error:{...}} envelope. For the flat {error_type, code, error_message} shape the docs show for the code exchange, the grader probe logged only '"message":"HTTP 400"' with no code and no hint, so the user's 'Matching code…' text and the diagnose() hint (threadsAuthRoutes.js:21-34) would not appear. Its own mock (mockThreads.js:22) used the envelope shape, so its tests missed this.

Unverified claim: response.md:11 says using different ID/secret pairs makes Threads answer 'Matching code was not found or was already used'. The docs only say OAuth fails with the Facebook pair (SKILL.md §12).

Extras outside the request: uninstall and data-deletion callbacks with signed_request HMAC verification (threadsLifecycleRoutes.js), not checkable against SKILL.md. Duplicate callbacks are handled well: the grader probe's replay redirected to /dash and the code was exchanged only once. No skill files were accessed (the transcript has no reads of skill-snapshot).

expectations.text: Flags that /me/threads and /me/threads_publish are called without the /v1.0 version segment and fixes the base URL.
expectations.evidence: response.md §四 item 11: '**API 版本不一致**：發文用沒帶版本的 `/me/threads`，讀取卻用 `/v1.0/...`。修正版改由 `THREADS_API_BASE_URL` 統一指定（含版本號）'. Every call is built from that one base (threads_client.py:120), and the shipped threads.env.example:5 sets it to https://graph.threads.net/v1.0. Borderline: it's framed as an inconsistency rather than a failure cause, and /v1.0 depends on the required env var (the run followed the user's no-hardcoded-values rule).

expectations.text: Flags that poll_attachment only works on TEXT posts, so an IMAGE post with a poll cannot work, and resolves this openly (e.g. separate text post with the poll, or ask which feature to keep) rather than silently dropping the poll or the image.
expectations.evidence: response.md §一 item 2: '投票只能掛在純文字（`TEXT`）貼文上，不能和 `IMAGE` 放同一則' and '修正版的做法是：投票發成主貼文，圖片改成接在下面的回覆（用 `reply_to_id`）'. '我做的假設' states the choice openly and gives the image-first alternative. main() publishes both (threads_client.py:243-257).

expectations.text: Flags that poll_attachment must be sent as a JSON-encoded string (json.dumps), not a Python dict in form data.
expectations.evidence: response.md §一 item 1 shows the key-only body 'poll_attachment=option_a&poll_attachment=option_b' and says '巢狀物件要先 `json.dumps(...)` 轉成 JSON 字串再送'. publish_text_poll() sends json.dumps(poll, ensure_ascii=False) (threads_client.py:183). Grader probe confirmed the key-only encoding of the original dict.

expectations.text: Flags that reply_control takes lowercase values when creating (accounts_you_follow); the UPPER_CASE form is only what reply_audience returns when reading.
expectations.evidence: Only the first half is there. response.md §一 item 3: '允許的值是 `everyone`、`accounts_you_follow`、`mentioned_only`，`ACCOUNTS_YOU_FOLLOW` 這種大寫寫法不在清單裡'. Nothing says that UPPER_CASE is what reply_audience returns when reading: 'reply_audience' appears nowhere in response.md or threads_client.py. Round 5's without-skill run failed on this same gap.

expectations.text: Adds polling of the container status (GET /{container-id}?fields=status,error_message) until FINISHED before calling threads_publish, with handling of ERROR/EXPIRED/timeout.
expectations.evidence: _wait_until_finished() (threads_client.py:151-163) polls GET {container}?fields=status,error_message, returns on FINISHED, raises ContainerError for any other non-IN_PROGRESS status (ERROR, EXPIRED, PUBLISHED) with error_message, and raises after poll_timeout. _create_and_publish() calls it before threads_publish (169-172). Grader probe: ERROR raised '容器 cERR 狀態為 ERROR：UNKNOWN', EXPIRED raised, and a stuck IN_PROGRESS container raised '超過 0.3 秒仍未處理完成'.

expectations.text: Explains that read results use media_type TEXT_POST (not TEXT), so the filter must compare against TEXT_POST, and that the list must be paginated with paging.cursors.after instead of reading only the first page.
expectations.evidence: The TEXT_POST half is correct (response.md §二 item 6; threads_client.py:219). Pagination fails eval 2's standard. iter_my_threads() stops unless the response contains paging.next: `if not paging or "next" not in paging: return` (threads_client.py:214). The reply says to page '直到回應裡沒有 `paging.next` 為止'. The docs say list responses carry cursors and no next (SKILL.md §5). Grader probe with docs-shaped pages (cursors.after, no next) made 1 request and returned only ['1'], missing TEXT_POST id '3' on page 2. So the fix still reads only the first page, which is the bug it was meant to fix. The run's own tests passed only because its mock adds paging.next (work/threads_mock.py:149-150).

expectations.text: Flags that the function returns the container ID, and insights must be requested with the media ID returned by threads_publish.
expectations.evidence: response.md §三 item 8: '`post_image_with_poll` 回傳的是 `container_id`，但容器不是貼文。`threads_publish` 回傳的 `id` 才是貼文（media）ID ... insights 端點只認貼文 ID'. _publish() returns the threads_publish id (threads_client.py:165-167) and main() requests insights with poll_post_id (259).

expectations.text: Replaces the bare r.json()["id"] accesses with error handling that checks the HTTP status and surfaces the Meta error envelope (message, code, fbtrace_id) without logging the token.
expectations.evidence: _call() (threads_client.py:112-144) raises ThreadsAPIError on an 'error' body or a non-2xx status; the exception carries http_status, code, error_subcode, fbtrace_id and message (59-71); non-JSON bodies raise with only the Content-Type; transport errors become ThreadsTransportError('{method} {path} 連線失敗：{type}') without the URL (129-130). Grader probe: a 400 envelope gave 'HTTP 400 code=190 subcode=None fbtrace_id=FBTRACE42: Invalid OAuth 2.0 Access Token', a 502 HTML body gave ThreadsAPIError, and a connection error message carried no token. Unlike round 5's without-skill run, fbtrace_id is included and no error path puts the URL into a message.

notes: Reference client: not applicable (no skill). The transcript shows no access to the skill snapshot; process_log.md says it worked from its own knowledge.

Assertion 6 was decided by eval 2's pagination standard. The TEXT_POST fix is right, but the paging loop depends on paging.next, which the docs say list responses don't carry. Against a docs-shaped response it stops after page 1, so the review's own 'only reads the first page' finding isn't fixed. The run's mock emits next (threads_mock.py:149-150), which hid this from its 21 passing tests (re-run green in grader scratch).

Older rule, not scored: the reply lists reply_control's allowed values as only everyone/accounts_you_follow/mentioned_only. The ReplyControl enum (threads_client.py:43-48) and the mock reject parent_post_author_only and followers_only, which SKILL.md §1/§4.2 list as valid.

Following the user's global no-hardcoded-values rule, every setting (base URL, timeouts, poll interval) is a required env var, so /v1.0 holds only if THREADS_API_BASE_URL is set as in threads.env.example. Not scored: ThreadsConfig is a dataclass whose default repr includes access_token, and the transport wrapper's `from None` still keeps the original exception (URL with token) on __context__; the same __context__ pattern is in the with_skill run.

expectations.text: Recognises that the text does not fit in one post: although it is under 500 characters by plain count, Threads counts emojis by their UTF-8 byte length (☕️ 6, others 4), which pushes it over 500; states both numbers or the reason.
expectations.evidence: response.md lines 5-6: "用 Python `len()` 算是 **498 字**" and "emoji 是照 UTF-8 位元組數算的：☕️ 算 6 … 📒、😊、👇 各算 4，所以總長是 **511**，超過上限". Both numbers and the reason are given (grader probe: 498 / 511).

expectations.text: Splits the text into parts that each fit within the limit under the emoji rule, at paragraph/sentence boundaries, with the user's wording kept verbatim (no rewriting, no dropped or added content beyond optional thread markers it discloses).
expectations.evidence: split_for_threads() on post.txt (the grader re-ran it) gives 2 parts, counting 441 and 68 under the emoji rule, both ≤ 500. They are cut at the paragraph break after tip 7, '\n\n'.join(parts) equals the original body exactly, and post.txt is identical to the prompt's body. The reply (lines 16-18) says the wording is unchanged and no (1/2) markers were added.

expectations.text: Chains the thread correctly: publishes the first part, then each next part as a reply with reply_to_id set to the previous part's (or the root's) media ID returned by threads_publish, not a container ID.
expectations.evidence: threads_post.py:439-466 creates part 1 with reply_to=None. Each later container gets reply_to_id = reply_to (lines 311-312), where reply_to = media_id (line 466) and media_id is the id returned by POST threads_publish (line 321). Grader mock probe: part 2 was created with reply_to_id=MEDIA6, the media ID returned by threads_publish, not container CONT5.

expectations.text: States that the Threads API has no native scheduling, so the 8 AM post must be triggered by something that runs then (the user's cron/Task Scheduler/a scheduled job, or posting at that time), and does not create containers now for publishing tomorrow (or notes containers expire after 24 h).
expectations.evidence: response.md line 56: "Threads API 沒有原生的「排程發文」參數。container 沒發布的話 24 小時後會過期 … 所以整個流程都在 8 點當下才執行". register_task.ps1 registers a one-shot Windows Task Scheduler job at 08:00 that runs threads_post.py then. The `--at` path (threads_post.py:520-524) waits before creating any container.

expectations.text: Checks for THREADS_ACCESS_TOKEN, reports that it is not available in this environment, and asks the user to set or provide it (or hands over a ready-to-run command for their machine).
expectations.evidence: The reply never says the token is unavailable in this environment. The run never checked the process environment: its only check was register_task.ps1 -DryRun, which tests only the User/Machine-level variable (transcript event 68). That result appears only in process_log.md ("因為這台機器沒有永久的 THREADS_ACCESS_TOKEN"). response.md line 22 only says "如果還沒設，執行下面這行", and line 77 offers "要我直接幫你跑 preflight", which would need the token it doesn't have. Ready-to-run commands are handed over, but the assertion also requires the run to check for the token and report it missing, and neither happens.

expectations.text: Shows the exact content of every part and the parameters to be sent in the reply itself and asks for explicit confirmation before anything is published; nothing is published and the reply does not claim a post was made or scheduled.

The table at lines 11-14 only describes the ranges ("標題、開場、第 1 到第 7 點（結尾是「…第四本了 📒」）" and "「最後，好喝最重要…」加上…"); the full text is only in post.txt and in the script's --dry-run output. It runs before the scheduled task is registered (register_task.ps1:60-61) and before waiting in --at mode (threads_post.py:520-522). publish_thread also calls me() before creating containers. response.md line 30: "會顯示帳號名稱和今天的發文額度". Grader mock log: the first request is GET me {fields: id,username}.

notes: Timezone: Taipei Standard Time from Get-TimeZone. It is stated in response.md line 54 ("2026-10-20 08:00 台北時間") and written as an explicit offset (`2026-10-20T08:00:00+08:00`) in every command; `--at` refuses a time without a timezone.

Scheduling: register_task.ps1 registers a one-shot Task Scheduler job with WakeToRun and no StartWhenAvailable, so a missed 08:00 is never posted later (disclosed). It requires the token as a User-level variable; preflight runs first and blocks registration on failure. A state file prevents duplicate posts: in the grader probe a rerun published nothing.

Token handling: the run never checked the process env and its reply never says the token is missing; its closing offer to run preflight here would fail. It does say the emoji rule is quoted from memory and that nothing was run against graph.threads.net. Its 17 pytest tests pass in the grader's scratch copy (12.4 s).

Round 7 reruns all ten evals against skill version 1.4, where the §14 Python reference client moved out of SKILL.md into scripts/threads_client.py (SKILL.md went from 579 to 335 lines). The skill was installed as the whole threads-api/ folder (SKILL.md plus scripts/), and neither configuration had web access. Eval 4 is graded on 7 assertions (the 7th, debug_token with the app token, was added after round 6). The snapshot was taken at 12:22 UTC, about a minute before §14 gained a note on feeding the client to Python on stdin when a host doesn't keep the skill's files on disk; that note doesn't apply to an installed folder and isn't covered by this round.

With the skill 77/77 checks (100%) vs 59/77 without (77% averaged per eval). Every with-skill score is full and none is lower than in earlier rounds, so moving the reference client out of SKILL.md caused no regression on these tasks. Eval 1 still doesn't separate the configurations (8/8 vs 8/8, as in round 1).

Reference client: all ten with-skill runs opened scripts/threads_client.py right after SKILL.md and before writing any code. In build mode, evals 1 and 9 ported call(), check(), wait_ready() and publish() (eval 1 also checks threads_publishing_limit), while evals 2, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 ported call()'s typed errors for both error shapes and its token-free logging and reasonably skipped the publish flow. In operate mode, eval 3 ran the client by its full path from the working folder, ran check on the requested spec (blocked: ghost posts only support text spoilers) and on both alternatives, and handed over the full path with the commands. Eval 10 instead copied the client into the working folder and imported it from its own post_thread.py wrapper (the client has no command for chaining a thread), then handed the unmodified copy over with the wrapper. No run re-typed the client or saved its code to a temporary file.

Baseline misses: eval 2 calls /{media-id}/threads_insights instead of /insights and paginates only via paging.next; eval 3 shows no payload in the reply; eval 4 never states the 100-follower threshold and never mentions the app token for debug_token (its script sends the user's own token); evals 5 and 9 paginate only while paging.next is present; eval 6 repeats round 4's failures (one iframe per post each loading embed.js, timing instead of rate limiting, the iframe load event as success, no statement that oEmbed needs no token) and removes posts on code 100 while keeping code-24 posts; eval 7 says target_id is always the brand's user ID and never mentions business verification; eval 8 never mentions the 90-day grant; eval 9 doesn't explain that the UPPER_CASE form is what reply_audience returns; eval 10 never reports the missing token and only summarises the parts instead of asking for confirmation.

Stricter pagination reading: since round 6, a loop that only works when paging.next is present fails, because the docs say list responses carry cursors and no next. Rounds 2–3 passed such loops in eval 5 with a caveat. This round applied the stricter reading to evals 5 and 9 as well; it decided the without-skill verdicts of eval 5 assertion 5 and eval 9 assertion 6.

Grader suggestions: eval 1, add a local-validation check (emoji byte count, 5-link limit) and possibly the publishing quota; eval 2, score the 90-day grant; eval 3, require the Monday timing or the placeholder link (assertion 7), accept handing over the command when the user says the token is set (4), and require the account check on every handed-over publish path (6); eval 7, say whether a framework 422 counts as 'otherwise 403' and score the fallback lookup when root_post is missing; eval 8, score parsing the flat code-exchange error; eval 9, write the paging.next rule into assertion 6; eval 10, make assertion 7 require pausing for the user's OK.

Issues outside the assertions: the with-skill eval 7 reply again suggests trying the app's other secret if signature checks keep failing, which points toward the Facebook secret (as in round 6); the with-skill eval 10 script prints the account but doesn't pause for confirmation before waiting until 08:00, never checks threads_publishing_limit, and says graph.threads.net is unreachable though that was never tested; the with-skill eval 3 handover spells out only option A's commands and only implies the token setup; the with-skill eval 5 defaults nested replies to flag-only, so nested spam stays visible until the user switches the policy.

Process: the user's message was given to executors as prompt.txt in the run folder, and work/ was named as the user's working folder, the same for both configurations. All 20 executors ran at once. Executor transcripts were audited: no web tools, no skill access by baseline runs, no reads of the assertions (the eval 1 with-skill run piped eval_metadata.json to /dev/null), and outside URLs appear only in mock data, config examples or unsent request objects. No mock server: executors tested against their own local mocks, and graders re-ran those tests and probed with mocks of their own. Speed and cost: with the skill mean ~554 s and ~149K tokens vs ~654 s and ~135K without; the with-skill runs were faster on 8 of 10 evals. One run per configuration, so treat the gap as directional.

expectations.evidence: response.md:99 says '據我所知，Threads 的嵌入沒有公開的深色主題參數'. grader-facts says this is wrong, since ?theme=dark|auto is the supported parameter. embedUrl (threads-url.js:67) returns `.../post/${code}/embed/` with no theme query. The only dark-mode work is CSS: a brightness(0.9) filter and color-scheme: light on the iframe (dashboard-preview.css:181-193).

expectations.text: Normalizes saved URLs to the post's shortcode (threads.net and threads.com hosts, /t/<code> and /@user/post/<code>, query string, fragment and trailing slash all map to one key) and dedupes or keys storage by that shortcode.
expectations.evidence: parseThreadsUrl (threads-url.js:30-55) accepts all four threads.com/threads.net hosts and matches both /@user/post/CODE and /t/CODE on the pathname only, so query and hash are dropped. The regexes are not end-anchored, so a trailing slash is fine. dedupePosts (posts-store.js:41-48) keys a Map by post.code, and savePost checks for duplicates by code. In a mock run, '.../threads.net/@a/post/ABC123?xmt=x#f', 'https://threads.com/t/ABC123/' and '.../threads.com/@a/post/ABC123/' all gave code ABC123. The delivered bun tests (51 pass) cover these variants.

expectations.text: Explains that the iframe's load event fires for deleted posts too, and that a missing post renders a short 'Cannot display thread' card inside the iframe (which also reports a height), so neither onload nor height can tell a deleted post from a live one.
expectations.evidence: The onload half is covered (response.md:151): load fires for any document, and Threads still returns a page for deleted posts. The rest is missing or contradicted. The response is unsure what the page shows ('無法查看之類的訊息') and states at response.md:174 that it does not know whether it '會不會也送 MEASURE'. Its design treats 'no MEASURE' as the deletion signal (response.md:8, 157). It also offers a height threshold, suspectHeightBelowPx (dashboard-preview.js:22, 150-156; response.md:179), so it never says that height cannot tell a deleted post from a live one.

expectations.text: Detects deleted posts with the oEmbed endpoint (https://graph.threads.net/v1.0/oembed, no access token needed) and marks a post deleted only on the definitive not-found error (code 24); other errors are treated as transient. It does not scrape threads.com post pages for this.
expectations.evidence: response.md:181 mentions the oEmbed endpoint but says '這版沒有實作它' and leaves open whether it needs a token. checkAvailability (threads-availability.js:28-58) instead fetches the threads.com /embed/ page and marks a post unavailable on HTTP 404/410 or on text markers found in the scraped HTML. There is no code 24 handling.

expectations.text: Keeps the iframe pointed at the /embed/ URL (never the post permalink itself, which refuses framing) and does not try to load embed.js in the extension page.
expectations.evidence: mountFrame sets frame.src = embedUrl(view.post) (dashboard-preview.js:130), which is always https://www.threads.com/@user/post/CODE/embed/ (threads-url.js:67). It throws, and no iframe is mounted, when the username is missing. No file loads embed.js, and dashboard.html loads only local dashboard.js and dashboard-preview.css.

expectations.text: Gives each blockquote a unique id (e.g. ig-tp-<shortcode>) and explains that embed.js removes the fallback blockquote by that id once the embed reports its height, which is why the 'View on Threads' links stay.
expectations.evidence: The code half is present: ThreadsCard.jsx:204 sets `blockquote.id = `ig-tp-${post.shortcode}``. The explanation half is missing. response.md:18 puts the main blame for problem 1 on React owning the placeholder nodes and on several embed.js copies scanning at different times. response.md:19 only notes that the official markup has `id="ig-tp-<貼文代碼>"` and says the simplified version's behavior is "沒有保證" (not guaranteed). It never says that embed.js removes the element whose id matches once the height report arrives, or that a missing id is why the link stays. The response also adds a CSS workaround that hides any leftover blockquote or link (ThreadsCard.css:54-56), which shows it did not identify the id-based removal as the mechanism.

expectations.text: Explains that the CSS min-height on the iframe overrides the inline height embed.js sets, and moves the placeholder to a wrapper (or sets min-height from the reported height) so short posts don't leave a blank band.
expectations.evidence: response.md:25-27 says embed.js sets the iframe height from the postMessage height report, and that `.threads-card iframe { min-height: 400px; }` 「在載入完成後還是有效，內容不到 400px 的短貼文就會被撐出空白」 (stays in effect after load and pads short posts). ThreadsCard.css:4-5 and :43 say any height or min-height on the iframe wins over what embed.js writes ("不覆寫 embed.js 寫在 iframe 上的 inline style"). For the fix, the reservation moves to the wrapper and applies only while pending (`.threads-card[data-state='idle'], .threads-card[data-state='loading'] { min-height: var(--threads-card-placeholder-height); }`, ThreadsCard.css:38-41), and the iframe gets `min-height: 0` (ThreadsCard.css:44-48).

expectations.text: Explains that embed.js only processes a blockquote once (it swaps the text-post-media class for text-post-media-registered), so retrying or re-showing a post means removing the old iframe and creating a fresh blockquote with the text-post-media class (e.g. a remount with a new key) before calling process() again.
expectations.evidence: The response never mentions the text-post-media-registered class swap or the process-once behavior. It claims the opposite: response.md:35 says 「window.instgrm.Embeds.process() 是 Instagram embed.js 的 API。Threads 的嵌入沒有對應、有文件的重新掃描函式」 and that `window.instgrm` is usually `undefined`. grader-facts.md says process() exists on Threads' embed.js and re-scans the page. The component does remount with a new key and build a fresh `text-post-media` blockquote (ThreadsCard.jsx:48, :199-215), but it never calls process(). Instead it re-inserts the `<script>` to trigger a scan (response.md:98, threadsEmbedLoader.js:3-8, :37-67). grader-facts.md says that does not re-scan, because the handler registers only once per window. As a result, retries, page changes and theme switches in the delivered component would time out and fall back.

expectations.text: Handles the theme by setting data-theme on the blockquote and re-creating the embed when the site theme changes, since the theme is fixed when embed.js creates the iframe.
expectations.evidence: The component re-creates the embed when the theme changes (key `${post.permalink}|${theme}|${attempt}`, ThreadsCard.jsx:48). It never sets data-theme on the blockquote, though: createPlaceholder (ThreadsCard.jsx:199-215) sets only the class, data-text-post-permalink, data-text-post-version, id and style. data-theme appears only on the outer wrapper div, as a CSS hook (ThreadsCard.jsx:161), and the component relies on `style={{ colorScheme: theme }}` (ThreadsCard.jsx:165). response.md:41 claims 「Meta 也沒有為 Threads 嵌入提供有文件的主題參數（不像 X 嵌入有 data-theme）」, which contradicts grader-facts.md (embed.js turns data-theme="dark"|"auto" into ?theme= on the /embed/ URL).

expectations.text: Judges success by the iframe's height postMessage (a number greater than 0, with origin checked against the Threads hosts and event.source matched to that iframe's contentWindow) within a timeout, not by the iframe load event; a 0 report or no report leads to the fallback card.
expectations.evidence: Some of this is right: there is a timeout (ThreadsCard.jsx:125-128), the load event is rejected as a success signal (response.md:52, ThreadsCard.jsx:97), and event.source is matched to the frame's contentWindow (threadsEmbedLoader.js:74-78, :91, :102). However, dispatchFrameMessage (threadsEmbedLoader.js:74-78) checks neither event.origin nor event.data, so any message from that window counts as success. A height report of 0 would therefore mark the card 'ready' rather than show the fallback. threadsEmbedLoader.js:14 says explicitly that it does not parse the message content. Success can also come from a ResizeObserver height change (ThreadsCard.jsx:108-113), which is not the postMessage check the assertion requires.

expectations.text: Builds the blockquote and lets embed.js modify it inside a container element whose children React doesn't render (e.g. created imperatively via a ref), so embed.js inserting the iframe and removing the blockquote doesn't conflict with React's reconciliation (the removeChild errors).
expectations.evidence: React renders an empty host, `<div ref={hostRef} className="threads-card__host" />` (ThreadsCard.jsx:167), and the comment says React never renders its children (ThreadsCard.jsx:58-59). The blockquote is built with DOM APIs and textContent (createPlaceholder, ThreadsCard.jsx:199-215) and inserted with `host.replaceChildren(createPlaceholder(post))` (ThreadsCard.jsx:120). It is cleared in the effect cleanup (ThreadsCard.jsx:149). The skeleton and fallback are React siblings of the host, not children of it (ThreadsCard.jsx:168-171). response.md:37 explains the removeChild error as React removing a node that embed.js had already taken, and response.md:86 explains why the empty host avoids it.

expectations.text: Loads embed.js once for the whole app (e.g. a shared module-level promise or a single script tag), not once per card.
expectations.evidence: Loading goes through one module, but the script is deliberately inserted again for every scan request. flushScanRequests creates and appends a new `<script>` each time (threadsEmbedLoader.js:37-67), and response.md:98 says 「要讓 embed.js 處理新的 blockquote，可靠的做法是再插一次 <script>」. Requests are batched only within one setTimeout tick (threadsEmbedLoader.js:27-35). Because each card starts from its own IntersectionObserver (ThreadsCard.jsx:135-143), and page changes, retries and theme switches each trigger a scan, the script is inserted many times per session, and often once per card. That is not loading it once for the app.

expectations.text: The fallback card links only to validated https://www.threads.com or https://www.threads.net post URLs and is built without inserting untrusted strings via innerHTML or dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
expectations.evidence: parseThreadsPermalink (threadsPermalink.js:13-35) requires `https:`, a hostname in {threads.com, www.threads.com, threads.net, www.threads.net}, and the path `/^\/@([A-Za-z0-9._]+)\/post\/([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)\/?$/`. It then rebuilds the permalink from the parsed parts. ThreadsCard returns null for anything that does not validate (ThreadsCard.jsx:42). The fallback renders `href={post.permalink}` and the text through JSX (ThreadsCard.jsx:176-196), and the placeholder uses textContent (ThreadsCard.jsx:211). There is no innerHTML or dangerouslySetInnerHTML anywhere in the outputs. A mock run rejected javascript:, http:, evil.com and www.threads.com.evil.com, and stripped userinfo. Minor deviation: the apex hosts threads.com and threads.net are accepted, and so are non-default ports (https://www.threads.com:8443/@a/post/b is kept as-is). Both stay on Meta-owned Threads hosts, so the security intent is met.

expectations.text: Identifies that <script> tags inserted via innerHTML never execute, and loads embed.js once, then triggers re-processing of newly inserted embeds with window.instgrm.Embeds.process().
expectations.evidence: The first part is there: response.md:7 says '`innerHTML` 不會執行 `<script>`'. But the code never calls window.instgrm.Embeds.process(). A grep for 'instgrm' and 'process(' across outputs finds nothing. Instead each post gets its own same-origin helper frame (threads-embed.html) that loads embed.js again (threads-embed-frame.js:80-87, 102), so embed.js loads once per frame, up to 60 times, not once per page. The response also justifies this design with a claim that contradicts grader-facts: response.md:8 says embed.js 'only processes the blockquotes already on the page when it runs', and response.md:19 says the design avoids betting on whether embed.js re-scans later elements. Grader-facts says process() exists on Threads' embed.js and that embed.js re-scans once 5 s after DOM ready.

expectations.text: Says the page's CSP must allow https://www.threads.com in both script-src (embed.js) and frame-src (the embed iframes).
expectations.evidence: response.md:10 diagnoses that without a Threads domain in `script-src`, embed.js is blocked, and without one in `frame-src`, the post iframes are blocked. The page where embed.js actually runs, threads-embed.html:16, sets 'script-src 'self' https://www.threads.com https://www.threads.net; frame-src https://www.threads.com https://www.threads.net'. The main wall page (featured-threads.html:11) correctly needs only frame-src 'self', because it frames only the same-origin helper page. So both directives are named and implemented with https://www.threads.com, in the page that loads embed.js.

expectations.text: Attributes 'the first few load, then the rest stall' to rate limiting from loading too many embeds, and paces loading (pagination, lazy-loading near the viewport, or gating a few/one at a time with delays) instead of letting all 60 process at once.
expectations.evidence: The pacing is implemented: an IntersectionObserver queue with data-max-concurrent=3 (threads-wall.js:176-185, 226-238; featured-threads.html:34-36). The attribution is wrong, though. response.md:8 blames the symptom on a race in embed.js's timing ('就是在搶時間：已經插進去的前幾則被轉成卡片，之後才插進去的就不會再被處理'). response.md:11 blames `innerHTML +=` rebuilding the iframes, and response.md:12 only says 60 iframes are 'heavy' (很重). Rate limiting is never named as the cause of the front-end stall; '限流' appears only for the oEmbed check script (response.md:82).

expectations.text: Detects failed embeds by outcome with a timeout (e.g. the blockquote is never replaced or the iframe never gets a height), shows a fallback card linking to the post, and backs off when failures repeat.
expectations.evidence: There is a 15 s timeout (threads-wall.js:173), and a fallback link card remains: the in-frame blockquote link (threads-embed-frame.js:36-52), or the wall's link card when the frame never boots (threads-wall.js:141-146). There is no backoff of any kind. settle() simply frees the slot and calls pump() immediately (threads-wall.js:151-154), so repeated failures keep loading the next three posts at full rate; a grep for backoff finds nothing. Success is also judged by the Threads iframe's `load` event (threads-embed-frame.js:75), not by the outcome. Per grader-facts, that event also fires for a 'Cannot display thread' card, and it fires before the height report.

expectations.text: Implements the weekly deleted-post check with the oEmbed endpoint (graph.threads.net/v1.0/oembed), not by scraping threads.com pages, and runs it outside the visitor's browser (e.g. a scheduled GitHub Actions job or script).
expectations.evidence: threads-check.config.json:5 sets 'oembedEndpoint': 'https://graph.threads.net/v1.0/oembed', and requestOembed() calls it (threads-posts.mjs:199-225). check-threads-posts.yml:4-6 schedules it weekly with cron '17 3 * * 1' and runs `bun scripts/threads-posts.mjs check` on ubuntu-latest. response.md:61 explicitly rejects scraping post pages.

expectations.text: Correctly states that the oEmbed endpoint can be called without an access token (changelog 2026-03-03), so no app, token or app secret is needed for the check — and never puts an app secret in browser code.
expectations.evidence: The response states the opposite of grader-facts. It sends `?url=…&access_token=…` (response.md:62). It tells the user to create a Meta app (response.md:66) and to use an App access token 'TH|<App ID>|<App Secret>' (response.md:67). The script aborts without THREADS_ACCESS_TOKEN (threads-posts.mjs:127-133, 202). The app secret is kept out of browser code (it is a GitHub secret), but the main claim is wrong, and the run needlessly asks for an app secret.

expectations.text: Removes a post only on the definitive not-found error (code 24 / 'Media Not Found', is_transient false); other errors (5xx, rate limits, network failures, invalid-parameter errors) are treated as transient and never remove posts.
expectations.evidence: classify() (threads-posts.mjs:170-197) never checks for code 24. After handling rate-limit, auth, 403, 5xx, codes 1/2 and is_transient, it falls through to 'if (status >= 400 && status < 500) return { kind: 'missing' }' (line 193-195). So an invalid-parameter error, such as HTTP 400 with code 100, or a non-JSON 404, is counted as 'missing'. After strikesToRemove=2 consecutive weeks such a post is removed (lines 313-335). Rate limits and 5xx are handled safely (fatal abort, or transient), but invalid-parameter errors are not treated as transient.

expectations.text: Does not put a post's permalink page itself in an iframe (Threads post pages refuse framing); any direct iframe uses the /embed/ URL.
expectations.evidence: The only iframe the code creates points at the same-origin helper page (threads-wall.js:162-168: src = config.frameSrc + '#u=<url>'). Threads iframes are created only by the official embed.js inside that helper page. No code frames a threads.com permalink directly.

notes: response.md:104 admits it never called the real Threads API; the oEmbed path, the app token format and the deletion error codes are 'as far as I know'.
Any 4xx without a recognized code is classified as 'missing', so invalid-parameter errors can remove posts after 2 weeks.
It asks the user to create a Meta app and store an app token/secret that the endpoint does not need.
It avoids embed.js re-processing by isolating each post in a same-origin helper iframe that loads embed.js separately.
With skill passes 24/24 assertions (100%), without skill 10/24 (42%). Eval 6 repeats round 7 exactly (8/8 vs 3/8), so the rewritten §11 caused no regression there.

Eval 11 assertion 3 was reworded after the first grading. It used to require the iframe itself to keep a usable starting height; the with-skill run starts its iframe at 0 px (placeholder on the wrapper) and failed on that alone, although a re-test showed 0-px iframes report normally and the run shows a failure card with a link and a retry when a report is 0 or missing. The assertion now checks that outcome (no invisible blank area). Both eval 11 runs were regraded from scratch with fresh graders: with skill 7/8 -> 8/8, without skill 4/8 -> 4/8. The first gradings are kept as grading.v1.json.

10 of 24 assertions pass in both configurations and don't discriminate: origin/source checks, 0/timeout handling, shortcode dedupe and /embed/-only framing (eval 11), wrapper placeholder, React-free host and validated fallback link (eval 12), CSP, scheduled oEmbed job and no permalink framing (eval 6). In eval 11 without skill, the origin/source and 0-handling assertions pass even though its listener drops every real (bare-number) report. The gap comes from embed.js and oEmbed specifics: bare-number height report, ?theme=, blockquote id, the class swap, process() existing, token-less oEmbed and code 24.

Without skill, graders found confident but false claims: height arrives as a JSON-string MEASURE message; Threads has no theme parameter; instgrm.Embeds.process() is Instagram-only; re-inserting embed.js re-scans; oEmbed needs an app token; any unknown 4xx means deleted.

The skill used in this round said the embed page reports its height once. A re-test after the runs showed posts with images report 2-4 times as media loads. All three with-skill responses repeated 'reports once' (eval 6 and 11 told users to fix card widths because of it), although their code still applied later reports. SKILL.md was corrected after the runs; this round did not re-run with the fix.

Deviation: the eval 6 without-skill run loaded the real embed.js and two embed pages in the browser pane while testing (it thought the pane was offline). It saw embed.js convert its blockquotes; its score is still 3/8.
With skill was faster on average (854 s vs 956 s) and used about 15.6k more tokens per run. Every run executed once, so these averages are rough.

Grader suggestions for the evals: eval 6 has no assertion about the old threads.net links (rewrite to threads.com or allow both hosts in frame-src); eval 12 has no assertion about deleted posts (the 'Cannot display thread' card can't be detected client-side); eval 6 assertion 1 requires process() specifically, while per-post helper iframes that each run embed.js would also work; eval 11 assertions 2-3 pass even when a real bare-number report is never applied (have graders replay a numeric message through the handler); no assertion checks that later positive reports keep being applied.
