expectations.evidence: response.md:21 explains that after the height report embed.js removes 'the element named by the blockquote's id', that official markup carries id="ig-tp-<shortcode>" and the user's doesn't, so the blockquote and link stay below the iframe. threadsEmbed.js:177 sets blockquote.id = `ig-tp-${shortcode}`. Uniqueness: response.md:23 and :145 say the id must be unique on the page, and CommunityPicks.jsx:13-27 dedupes by shortcode. A mock run of mountThreadsEmbed confirmed the generated blockquote has id 'ig-tp-ABC'.

expectations.text: Explains that the CSS min-height on the iframe overrides the inline height embed.js sets, and moves the placeholder to a wrapper (or sets min-height from the reported height) so short posts don't leave a blank band.
expectations.evidence: response.md:27 says embed.js sets the iframe's style.height, a CSS min-height wins over height, so `.threads-card iframe { min-height: 400px }` stretches every post shorter than 400 px. response.md:29 moves the placeholder to the outer container and applies it only while loading. ThreadsCard.css:25-28 sets min-height on .threads-card only for data-status waiting/loading, and ThreadsCard.css:30-33 has no height on the iframe.

expectations.text: Explains that embed.js only processes a blockquote once (it swaps the text-post-media class for text-post-media-registered), so retrying or re-showing a post means removing the old iframe and creating a fresh blockquote with the text-post-media class (e.g. a remount with a new key) before calling process() again.
expectations.evidence: response.md:35 says each blockquote is processed once: the iframe takes the text-post-media class and the blockquote becomes text-post-media-registered, and process() only finds blockquotes that still have text-post-media. response.md:46 gives the fix as 'clear the container, build a brand-new blockquote, then call process()'. In the code, retry bumps `attempt` (ThreadsCard.jsx:111-114, dep at :98). Cleanup calls host.replaceChildren(), which removes the old iframe (:96). mountThreadsEmbed then calls host.replaceChildren(buildBlockquote(...)) with className 'text-post-media' before window.instgrm.Embeds.process() (threadsEmbed.js:174, :252, :256). The list keys on shortcode (CommunityPicks.jsx:39).

expectations.text: Handles the theme by setting data-theme on the blockquote and re-creating the embed when the site theme changes, since the theme is fixed when embed.js creates the iframe.
expectations.evidence: response.md:52 says the theme is decided when the iframe is created: data-theme="dark" makes embed.js append ?theme=dark and use a transparent background. response.md:54-56 says the only fix is to rebuild with a new data-theme, so theme is an effect dependency. threadsEmbed.js:181 sets data-theme='dark' when theme is dark. ThreadsCard.jsx:98 lists `theme` in the layout-effect deps, so cleanup clears the host and the embed is re-mounted. response.md:57 also rejects data-theme="auto" because it follows the OS, not the site toggle.

expectations.text: Judges success by the iframe's height postMessage (a number greater than 0, with origin checked against the Threads hosts and event.source matched to that iframe's contentWindow) within a timeout, not by the iframe load event; a 0 report or no report leads to the fallback card.
expectations.evidence: threadsEmbed.js:224-232 drops any message whose origin is not in messageOrigins ['https://www.threads.com','https://www.threads.net'] (threadsEmbedConfig.js:12) or whose source is not host.querySelector('iframe').contentWindow. toHeight accepts a bare number (:193-197). height > 0 resolves 'loaded' and 0 resolves 'failed'. A 12 s timer (:234-244, firstReportTimeoutMs) resolves 'failed'. On failure ThreadsCard.jsx:50-54/:75 clears the host and sets status 'failed', which renders ThreadsFallback (:121). response.md:62-72 explicitly rejects onload. Mock replay: bare 498 from www.threads.com gave {status:'loaded',height:498}; 0 gave {status:'failed',reason:'zero-height'}; a wrong origin and a wrong event.source were both ignored (still pending); 300 from www.threads.net gave loaded.

expectations.text: Builds the blockquote and lets embed.js modify it inside a container element whose children React doesn't render (e.g. created imperatively via a ref), so embed.js inserting the iframe and removing the blockquote doesn't conflict with React's reconciliation (the removeChild errors).
expectations.evidence: ThreadsCard.jsx:119 renders `<div ref={hostRef} className="threads-card__embed" />` with no React children, and the comment says it must never have any. The blockquote and link are created with document.createElement and inserted via host.replaceChildren (threadsEmbed.js:172-190, :252). The skeleton and fallback are React siblings outside the host. response.md:40 explains the removeChild error: embed.js inserts, re-classes and deletes nodes React manages, and React then tries to remove or move a node that has moved.

expectations.text: Loads embed.js once for the whole app (e.g. a shared module-level promise or a single script tag), not once per card.
expectations.evidence: threadsEmbed.js:39-86 has a module-level `scriptPromise`. loadThreadsEmbedScript() returns early if instgrm.Embeds.process exists or a promise is pending, reuses an existing script tag, and inserts a single <script> into document.head. The script is only removed and retried after a failure (:60-65, :89-94). response.md:47 and :106 say embed.js is loaded once and the per-card script insertion should be deleted.

expectations.text: The fallback card links only to validated https://www.threads.com or https://www.threads.net post URLs and is built without inserting untrusted strings via innerHTML or dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
expectations.evidence: parseThreadsPostUrl (threadsEmbed.js:18-33) parses with new URL and allows only the threads.com, www.threads.com, threads.net and www.threads.net hostnames. The path must match /@user/post/<code> or /t/<code> with restricted character classes. The permalink is rebuilt as 'https://www.threads.com' + path, so output is always https even for http input. ThreadsFallback (ThreadsCard.jsx:147-151) renders `<a href={permalink}>` only when permalink is non-null, through JSX. The mock showed javascript:alert(1) and threads.com.evil.com both return null, and an http threads.net URL is rewritten to https://www.threads.com/@a.b/post/XyZ_1. A grep of the outputs found no innerHTML, dangerouslySetInnerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML or outerHTML in the code.

expectations.text: Points out that a deleted or unavailable post still renders a 'Cannot display thread' card that reports a height, so client-side success detection counts it as loaded, and recommends pruning such posts with the oEmbed endpoint (code 24 means gone), e.g. on the backend or in a scheduled job.
expectations.evidence: response.md:64 says deleted or non-embeddable posts still load the embed page (showing 'Cannot display thread') and fire load. response.md:74 says that card also reports about 190 px, so height alone can't tell it from a short text post, and points to backend oEmbed checks. response.md:179 says the frontend can't distinguish the two. response.md:177-186 recommends a periodic (e.g. daily) backend oEmbed call per URL and removing the post on HTTP 400 code 24 (subcode 4279056). It also states no token is needed and the 1,000/hour limit, both of which match grader-facts.

notes: Not tested in a real browser against threads.com (no network). The embed.js behaviors relied on are observed, not documented (response.md:160-166).
The fallback copy names 'post deleted' as a cause of a timeout or 0 report, which contradicts how deleted posts actually behave.

expectations.text: Identifies that <script> tags inserted via innerHTML never execute, and loads embed.js once, then triggers re-processing of newly inserted embeds with window.instgrm.Embeds.process().
expectations.evidence: response.md:7 states the cause outright: "用 innerHTML 插入的 `<script>` 不會執行". assets/featured-wall.js:157-177 (loadEmbedScript) returns the existing window.instgrm.Embeds if it is already there. Otherwise it appends a single <script> and resolves only after checking that Embeds.process is a function. featured-wall.js:335-337 adds class text-post-media to the newly built blockquote and calls embeds.process(). response.md:43 tells the user to delete every other embed.js tag so that two copies don't compete.

expectations.text: Says the page's CSP must allow https://www.threads.com in both script-src (embed.js) and frame-src (the embed iframes).
expectations.evidence: response.md:10: "CSP 要在 `script-src` 和 `frame-src` 都放行 `https://www.threads.com`，少一個就會整片失效". response.md:38-41 gives the exact snippet "script-src 'self' https://www.threads.com; frame-src https://www.threads.com". featured.html:6-13 contains the same comment and a meta CSP that includes both.

expectations.text: Attributes 'the first few load, then the rest stall' to rate limiting from loading too many embeds, and paces loading (pagination, lazy-loading near the viewport, or gating a few/one at a time with delays) instead of letting all 60 process at once.
expectations.evidence: response.md:8: "一次 60 則會被 Threads 限流…連續載幾十個還是會被回 HTTP 429…看起來就是「後面整排卡住」". On pacing, featured-wall.js:405-415 uses an IntersectionObserver with a 600px rootMargin, so only cards near the viewport become eligible. runScheduler (featured-wall.js:375-403) loads one card at a time and sleeps gapMs (3600 ms, featured.html:43) between cards. Blockquotes get the text-post-media class only when their turn comes (featured-wall.js:335), so embed.js never sees all 60 at once.

expectations.text: Detects failed embeds by outcome with a timeout (e.g. the blockquote is never replaced or the iframe never gets a height), shows a fallback card linking to the post, and backs off when failures repeat.
expectations.evidence: Outcome and timeout: an attempt fails if the iframe's first postMessage height is 0 (featured-wall.js:300-301) or if no height arrives within reportTimeoutMs = 12000 (featured-wall.js:327-330 and 349-362). Fallback: showFailure (featured-wall.js:235-261) removes the dead iframe and shows a card with a link to the post ("在 Threads 查看"), the possible causes and a retry button. Back-off: after 3 consecutive failures the loop pauses for pauseMs (60 s), multiplying the pause by 1.5 up to 5 min and the per-card gap by 1.5 up to 10 s (featured-wall.js:390-398). Caveat: on timeout, judgeTimeout counts an iframe whose getBoundingClientRect().height > 0 as a success. That measurement includes borders, so if embed.js gives its 0-height iframe a CSS border, a stalled embed could be marked OK. I could not check embed.js's iframe styling offline, so this does not change the verdict.

expectations.text: Implements the weekly deleted-post check with the oEmbed endpoint (graph.threads.net/v1.0/oembed), not by scraping threads.com pages, and runs it outside the visitor's browser (e.g. a scheduled GitHub Actions job or script).
expectations.evidence: .github/workflows/check-threads-posts.yml:6-8 sets a weekly cron ('17 1 * * 1') plus workflow_dispatch, and line 33 sets THREADS_OEMBED_ENDPOINT: https://graph.threads.net/v1.0/oembed. scripts/check-threads-posts.mjs:58-101 (askOembed) only calls that endpoint and never fetches threads.com pages. The job runs on ubuntu-latest, not in the visitor's browser.

expectations.text: Correctly states that the oEmbed endpoint can be called without an access token (changelog 2026-03-03), so no app, token or app secret is needed for the check — and never puts an app secret in browser code.
expectations.evidence: response.md:56: "這個端點目前不需要 token". response.md:86: "oEmbed 依 changelog 從 2026-03-03 起就不需要 token". scripts/check-threads-posts.mjs:44-47 treats THREADS_APP_TOKEN as optional, and the workflow runs without it. No browser file (featured.html, featured-wall.js, threads-url.js) contains or asks for a token or secret. The response does offer an optional fallback: it suggests storing TH|<APP_ID>|<APP_SECRET> in GitHub Secrets if 190/104 or 429 errors appear, citing that the App Access Tokens docs page still says a token is required. This fallback is server-side only and secret-scoped, so it doesn't break the 'never in browser code' clause, and the main statement that no token is needed is correct per grader-facts.

expectations.text: Removes a post only on the definitive not-found error (code 24 / 'Media Not Found', is_transient false); other errors (5xx, rate limits, network failures, invalid-parameter errors) are treated as transient and never remove posts.
expectations.evidence: The code removes a post only when code === 24 (check-threads-posts.mjs:96), and only if a recheck after CONFIRM_DELAY_MS also returns code 24 (lines 189-202). code 100/2207047 is classed as 'invalid' and kept (line 97). 429 or rate-limit codes and auth codes throw StopRun before any write (lines 98-99, 103-113). Everything else is classed as 'transient' and kept (line 100). I confirmed this with a Bun mock oEmbed server in the scratchpad. A code-24 post and its threads.net duplicate were removed. A post that returned 24 first and then OK, a 500, a 502 non-JSON response, 100/2207047, plain 100, and an unparseable URL were all kept. A 429 mid-run exited 1 and left the file byte-identical. Connection refused was classed as transient, exited 1, and left the file unchanged. The script doesn't read is_transient, but code 24 is exactly the definitive not-found error described in grader-facts.

expectations.text: Does not put a post's permalink page itself in an iframe (Threads post pages refuse framing); any direct iframe uses the /embed/ URL.
expectations.evidence: None of the delivered code creates an iframe. featured-wall.js only builds blockquote.text-post-media elements with data-text-post-permalink (lines 216-227, 335), and embed.js creates the /embed/ iframes. featured-wall.js:263-265 and 271-281 only read the iframe and set its style.height. No permalink is set as an iframe src anywhere.

expectations.text: Handles the old threads.net links so their embeds aren't blocked: either rewrites them to https://www.threads.com before building the embed (e.g. from the shortcode), or allows both https://www.threads.com and https://www.threads.net in the CSP's frame-src (and script-src where needed).
expectations.evidence: assets/threads-url.js:7-32 accepts threads.net and threads.com hosts, extracts the shortcode and returns permalink `https://www.threads.com/t/${shortcode}`. featured-wall.js:142 and 219 use that rewritten permalink for data-text-post-permalink, so every iframe is on www.threads.com. response.md:9 explains why: threads.net permalinks would produce www.threads.net iframes, which a threads.com-only frame-src blocks. response.md:42 notes that frame-src therefore doesn't need threads.net.

notes: The response notes that the embed.js behaviours it relies on (class swap, bare-number postMessage, removal by id, 3-at-a-time) were observed rather than documented.
The response is unsure whether style-src 'self' in the sample CSP blocks embed.js inline styles.
If oEmbed starts rejecting tokenless calls or the shared runner IP gets rate-limited, the response suggests an optional THREADS_APP_TOKEN GitHub secret.

expectations.text: States that the /embed/ page does send its height via postMessage, as a bare number (or numeric string) rather than an object, so the MEASURE listener never matches; fixes the listener to read the number and does not inject a content script into the iframe to measure it.
expectations.evidence: response.md:5 and :34 say the data is a JSON string: '最可能的原因是送來的 e.data 是 JSON 字串' / "Instagram 送的是 '{\"type\":\"MEASURE\",\"details\":{\"height\":612}}' 這種 JSON 字串". Per grader-facts the page sends a bare number. lib/embed-height.js:31-48 readEmbedHeight only accepts MEASURE objects/JSON strings and a probe object; for a number it hits `if (!msg || typeof msg !== 'object') return null`. Mock replay of 498, 534, 574, '498', 194 through createEmbedHeightRouter applied no heights ([]). The response also ships a content-script measuring fallback (optional/embed-height-probe.js, optional/manifest.content-scripts.json) and tells the user to fall back to it if no messages arrive (response.md:46-53).

expectations.text: The message listener checks event.origin against the Threads hosts (https://www.threads.com, plus https://www.threads.net if threads.net iframes can occur) and matches event.source to the iframe's contentWindow before applying a height.
expectations.evidence: lib/embed-height.js:13 THREADS_ORIGIN_RE = /^https:\/\/(?:www\.)?threads\.(?:com|net)$/; onMessage returns early if !isThreadsOrigin(event.origin) (:70-75), then findHandler compares iframe.contentWindow === source (:61-67) and returns if no handler (:89) before calling handler(height). Mock replay: object messages from https://evil.example and from an unregistered source were dropped; www.threads.com / www.threads.net accepted. (It also accepts bare threads.com/threads.net without www, a harmless broadening.)

expectations.text: A height report of 0, or no report within a timeout, never leaves the preview as an invisible or blank area with nothing else shown: the 0 is not applied as the final height (ignored or treated as a failure), and the card shows something usable instead, such as a placeholder or starting height, or a failure card with a link to the post or a retry.
expectations.evidence: 0 is never applied: toPositiveNumber requires n > 0 (embed-height.js:19-22) and the router drops heights below minHeightPx 60 (:90, config.js:25); a bare 0 is dropped as well (replay). The frame starts at initialHeightPx 240 with a '載入預覽中…' placeholder (dashboard.js:109,180; dashboard.css:193-201). If no height arrives within heightTimeoutMs 6000 after load, markUnmeasured sets a 560px resizable frame and shows the hint '沒有收到這則預覽的高度回報，可以拖曳預覽框右下角調整高度。' (dashboard.js:129-134,143; dashboard.html:33). Every card also has a header link to the post (dashboard.js:96-99).

expectations.text: Fixes dark mode by adding ?theme=dark (or ?theme=auto) to the /embed/ iframe URL.
expectations.evidence: No theme parameter anywhere (grep for 'theme' finds only response.md:61). config.js:15 urlParams: {}. response.md:61 states the opposite of the ground truth: '就我所知，Threads 嵌入目前沒有深色主題參數'. The only change is `color-scheme: light` on the iframe element (dashboard.css:226) plus a dark skeleton, which keeps the card white.

expectations.text: Normalizes saved URLs to the post's shortcode (threads.net and threads.com hosts, /t/<code> and /@user/post/<code>, query string, fragment and trailing slash all map to one key) and dedupes or keys storage by that shortcode.
expectations.evidence: lib/threads-url.js:16 host regex accepts (www.)threads.com|net; :51 splits pathname with filter(Boolean) (trailing slash) and ignores query/hash; :54-66 handle /@user/post/CODE and /t/CODE, returning { code }. groupSavedPosts groups by ref.code (:111-134) for display, and compactSavedPosts writes a deduped list back to storage (:159-197; dashboard.js:330-357). tests/run-tests.mjs:35-51 covers threads.net/.com, /t/, ?xmt=, #comments, trailing slash, /embed/; I ran `bun tests/run-tests.mjs` and all 17 tests passed.

expectations.text: Explains that the iframe's load event fires for deleted posts too, and that a missing post renders a short 'Cannot display thread' card inside the iframe (which also reports a height), so neither onload nor height can tell a deleted post from a live one.
expectations.evidence: Covers only the load half: response.md:94 'iframe 的 load 事件只代表「有一份文件載入完成」。Threads 回的「這則貼文無法顯示」頁面也是一份正常載入的文件'. It never says the not-found card also reports a height or that height cannot distinguish it; its argument is only about cross-origin content and status codes being unreadable.

expectations.text: Detects deleted posts with the oEmbed endpoint (https://graph.threads.net/v1.0/oembed, no access token needed) and marks a post deleted only on the definitive not-found error (code 24); other errors are treated as transient. It does not scrape threads.com post pages for this.
expectations.evidence: lib/post-status.js:100-121 fetches the threads.com post permalink (canonicalPostUrl) with credentials:'omit', marks 404/410 as gone and parses og:url from the HTML (classifyPostHtml :75-86). That is scraping threads.com post pages, with optional host permissions requested for it (manifest.json:7-10). oEmbed is only mentioned as a backend alternative, with a hedge that a token may be needed: response.md:111 '不過需不需要 token、配額多少，請以 Meta 的文件為準，而且 token 不能放在擴充功能裡'. No code 24 handling.

expectations.text: Keeps the iframe pointed at the /embed/ URL (never the post permalink itself, which refuses framing) and does not try to load embed.js in the extension page.

No embed.js script in dashboard.html or any JS. The only embed.js mention is about inspecting it on a separate localhost/https test page (response.md:45).

expectations.text: Keeps applying every later height report above 0 from the same iframe (posts with images report again as their media loads) instead of stopping after the first one, and does not tell the user that the page reports its height only once.

But the real reports are bare numbers, and readEmbedHeight returns null for them, so the delivered handler applies none of them. Replaying 498 -> 534 -> 574 applied nothing ([]). It also drops any report from 1 to 59 px (minHeightPx 60, embed-height.js:90), so not every report above 0 is applied. The response never claims the page reports only once, but it does not keep applying the real reports.

notes: The response admits it could not verify the height-message format, whether /t/<code>/embed/ works, or the deleted-post HTTP status and og:url (response.md:129-134).
Without a theme parameter, the response says the card stays white wherever the embed's own body is white.
The deleted-post check scrapes threads.com permalinks and needs optional host permissions. It is unverified, and the response asks the user to calibrate it with debugCheck().
A content-script height probe is shipped as an opt-in fallback.
After a 6 s timeout the frame becomes manually resizable at 560px. Because the handler drops real bare-number reports, this is effectively the path every card will take.

expectations.evidence: createPlaceholder (mountThreadsEmbed.js:189-204) sets class, data-text-post-permalink and data-text-post-version but no id. expectations.evidence: ThreadsCard.jsx:95-96 renders an empty '<div ref={hostRef} className="threads-card__host" />' with the comment that React never puts children in it. mountThreadsEmbed appends an imperatively created same-origin iframe to that host (mountThreadsEmbed.js:41-45, 145) and builds the blockquote and embed.js script inside that iframe's document via DOM APIs (mountThreadsEmbed.js:96-102), so embed.js never touches React-owned nodes. response.md:38 links the removeChild error to React removing a node embed.js has already moved out from under it.

expectations.text: Loads embed.js once for the whole app (e.g. a shared module-level promise or a single script tag), not once per card.
expectations.evidence: The design loads embed.js once per card, in each card's own iframe document: response.md:71 '每張卡在自己的同源 iframe 裡載入一次 embed.js' and response.md:83 'embed.js 每張卡執行一次，下載走瀏覽器快取'. Code: build() appends a new <script src=CONFIG.scriptSrc> for every mount (mountThreadsEmbed.js:97-102). It also tells the user to remove embed.js from the main page (response.md:611).

expectations.text: The fallback card links only to validated https://www.threads.com or https://www.threads.net post URLs and is built without inserting untrusted strings via innerHTML or dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
expectations.evidence: The fallback href is the permalink from toThreadsPermalink (threadsPermalink.js:15-35): it parses with URL, allows only threads.com/threads.net hosts (apex or www), requires the path /@user/post/code, and always rebuilds the URL as 'https://${hostname}/@user/post/code', dropping query and hash. An invalid URL produces a fallback with no link (ThreadsCard.jsx:43-48, 111). The fallback is plain JSX text (ThreadsCard.jsx:105-124); the blockquote uses setAttribute/textContent (mountThreadsEmbed.js:189-204); the only doc.write is the constant FRAME_HTML (mountThreadsEmbed.js:3, 165). There is no innerHTML or dangerouslySetInnerHTML. One nuance: the apex hosts (https://threads.com/...) are also accepted, but these are Threads-owned hosts and the spirit of the check is met.

expectations.text: Points out that a deleted or unavailable post still renders a 'Cannot display thread' card that reports a height, so client-side success detection counts it as loaded, and recommends pruning such posts with the oEmbed endpoint (code 24 means gone), e.g. on the backend or in a scheduled job.
expectations.evidence: The first half is present: response.md:63 '被刪除或改成私人的貼文，Threads 可能回一張「無法顯示」的內嵌頁，它同樣會回報高度，前端分不出來。這種情況要靠後台定期檢查清單裡的網址是否還能公開瀏覽，把失效的移除。' It never mentions the oEmbed endpoint or error code 24, so it gives no concrete way to detect a gone post.

expectations.text: Identifies that <script> tags inserted via innerHTML never execute, and loads embed.js once, then triggers re-processing of newly inserted embeds with window.instgrm.Embeds.process().
expectations.evidence: The first half is met: response.md:7-8 says scripts inserted via innerHTML do not execute. The rest is not. The response never calls window.instgrm.Embeds.process() (grep for 'instgrm' and 'process(' across outputs finds nothing). It also says the opposite: response.md:11 states "官方沒有公開「請重新掃描」的 API，這條路靠不住". grader-facts says process() exists and re-scans for blockquote.text-post-media. Instead of loading embed.js once, the design loads it separately in each of the 60 same-origin embed-frame.html frames (embed-frame.js:105-110).

expectations.text: Says the page's CSP must allow https://www.threads.com in both script-src (embed.js) and frame-src (the embed iframes).
expectations.evidence: response.md:18: "要嵌入，CSP 得同時放行 embed.js 的網域（script-src）和貼文 iframe 的網域（frame-src）。Threads 已經從 threads.net 搬到 threads.com…". In the delivered design the document that runs embed.js is embed-frame.html, and its CSP (embed-frame.html:5) has "script-src 'self' https://www.threads.com https://www.threads.net; frame-src https://www.threads.com https://www.threads.net". The main page only needs frame-src 'self' (index.html:5), and that holds for this nested-frame architecture.

expectations.text: Attributes 'the first few load, then the rest stall' to rate limiting from loading too many embeds, and paces loading (pagination, lazy-loading near the viewport, or gating a few/one at a time with delays) instead of letting all 60 process at once.
expectations.evidence: response.md:14-15 under "60 個 iframe 同時載入": "一次全部開，連線會塞住，也容易被 Threads 限流…看起來就像整排停住". This ties the stall to loading too many embeds at once, including rate limiting. Note that the 'first few appear' part is put down mainly to a timing difference (response.md:10-11), so the rate-limit attribution is one of several causes rather than the headline. Pacing is clearly implemented. An IntersectionObserver queues a card only when it nears the viewport (threads-wall.js:262-273, rootMargin from data-preload-margin="600px 0px"). A concurrency queue allows at most data-max-concurrent=3 (load-queue.js:19-41, index.html:29). Placeholder min-height keeps all 60 from intersecting at once (threads-wall.css:29-35).

expectations.text: Detects failed embeds by outcome with a timeout (e.g. the blockquote is never replaced or the iframe never gets a height), shows a fallback card linking to the post, and backs off when failures repeat.
expectations.evidence: Timeout and fallback exist. Each item has a 20 s timer (threads-wall.js:207-211). Success is signalled when the inner Threads iframe fires 'load' (embed-frame.js:57). On timeout the card shows a 'slow' fallback with an "在 Threads 查看 @author 的貼文" link and a retry button (threads-wall.js:127-139, threads-wall.css:69-73). There is no backoff. item.attempts is incremented (threads-wall.js:195) but never read. On timeout the slot is released immediately, so the next item starts while the slow iframe keeps loading (threads-wall.js:208-210). Nothing slows down or pauses after repeated failures. Also, per grader-facts the iframe 'load' event fires even for a missing post's 'Cannot display thread' card, so the success signal is weak.

expectations.text: Implements the weekly deleted-post check with the oEmbed endpoint (graph.threads.net/v1.0/oembed), not by scraping threads.com pages, and runs it outside the visitor's browser (e.g. a scheduled GitHub Actions job or script).
expectations.evidence: It does run outside the browser, in a weekly GitHub Actions job (threads-featured-check.yml:11-14), and it does not scrape pages. But it does not use oEmbed. It lists the token owner's posts via GET /me/threads and /me/replies and treats featured posts missing from that list as deleted (check-deleted-posts.js:26-46, response.md:115-117). No 'oembed' string appears anywhere in the outputs.

expectations.text: Correctly states that the oEmbed endpoint can be called without an access token (changelog 2026-03-03), so no app, token or app secret is needed for the check — and never puts an app secret in browser code.
expectations.evidence: oEmbed is never mentioned. The response requires the opposite setup: a Meta App with threads_basic + threads_read_replies, a long-lived token obtained with the app secret (response.md:141-147: "client_secret=<App 密鑰>"), a THREADS_ACCESS_TOKEN secret, and a PAT with Secrets write access for token refresh (response.md:149-153). It also wrongly claims other people's posts cannot be checked (response.md:137: "別人的貼文，Threads API 沒有可靠的查法"), although grader-facts says tokenless oEmbed works for any post. The app secret is not in browser code, but the main claim is absent.

expectations.text: Removes a post only on the definitive not-found error (code 24 / 'Media Not Found', is_transient false); other errors (5xx, rate limits, network failures, invalid-parameter errors) are treated as transient and never remove posts.
expectations.evidence: The removal criterion is absence from the /me/threads + /me/replies listing for missThreshold=2 consecutive runs (plan.js:64-89, config.json:7). It is not a code 24 / is_transient:false error. Error codes are never used to decide deletion. API errors do abort the run without changes (threads-client.js:71-80, check-deleted-posts.js:168-176), which is safe, but the required definitive-signal logic is not implemented. Non-owner posts are never checked at all.

expectations.text: Does not put a post's permalink page itself in an iframe (Threads post pages refuse framing); any direct iframe uses the /embed/ URL.
expectations.evidence: The only iframe the code creates is the same-origin embed-frame.html, with the permalink passed in the hash (threads-wall.js:198-205: src.hash = new URLSearchParams({ id, u: item.permalink })). Inside it, embed.js builds the Threads iframe from a blockquote with data-text-post-permalink (embed-frame.js:67-81), and embed.js uses the /embed/ URL. No code frames a Threads permalink directly.

expectations.text: Handles the old threads.net links so their embeds aren't blocked: either rewrites them to https://www.threads.com before building the embed (e.g. from the shortcode), or allows both https://www.threads.com and https://www.threads.net in the CSP's frame-src (and script-src where needed).
expectations.evidence: Both are done. The front end rebuilds every permalink from author + shortcode on data-permalink-origin="https://www.threads.com" (threads-wall.js:107 buildPermalink(permalinkOrigin, parsed.author, parsed.shortcode); index.html:28). normalize-posts.js rewrites threads.net to threads.com in posts.json (normalize.js:84). embed-frame.html:5 lists both www.threads.com and www.threads.net in script-src and frame-src. One caveat: /t/<code> links are rejected as un-embeddable (threads-wall.js:89-95). That is wrong per grader-facts, but it does not affect the .net to .com handling.

notes: Round 9 reruns evals 6, 11 and 12 against the SKILL.md that will ship as 1.5: §11 rewritten from two production projects and live tests, the 'reports its height once' claim corrected (image posts report 2-4 times), and the official-docs sync of 2026-10-23. Each eval gained a 9th assertion after round 8 (27 in total). Neither configuration had internet access, and this round the runs were also told not to open web pages with any browser tool; none reported doing so.
With skill passes 27/27 (100%), without skill 11/27 (41%): eval 6 9/9 vs 4/9, eval 11 9/9 vs 4/9, eval 12 9/9 vs 3/9.

The 'reports once' fix took effect. Eval 11 with skill applies every report above 0 (the grader replayed 534, then 574, then '600' through the delivered handler and all three were applied) and passes the new 9th assertion; none of the three with-skill responses tells the user the page reports only once (round 8: all three did). Eval 11 without skill again parses the height as a JSON-string MEASURE message, so replaying 498, 534 and 574 applied nothing and its 9th assertion fails.

New 9th assertions: eval 6 (old threads.net links) passes in both configurations and doesn't discriminate this round; eval 11 (keep applying later reports) and eval 12 (a deleted post's 'Cannot display thread' card looks like success, so prune with oEmbed code 24) pass with skill and fail without.

Without skill, the same confident but false claims as round 8 came back: Threads has no theme parameter (evals 11, 12), there is no re-scan API / process() is Instagram's (evals 6, 12), the height arrives as a JSON-string MEASURE message (eval 11). For deleted posts it listed the user's own posts through the API (eval 6, needing an app, a token and a secrets-write PAT) or scraped threads.com pages (eval 11) instead of token-less oEmbed.

Grader suggestions for the evals: split eval 6 assertion 1 into 'diagnoses that innerHTML scripts don't run' and 'doesn't claim there is no re-scan API', so a per-post wrapper-iframe design isn't failed the same way as a wrong fix; reword eval 12 assertion 7 to 'doesn't rely on re-inserting embed.js into the same document'; make eval 11 assertion 9 replay real bare-number reports; tighten eval 11's oEmbed assertion around reading the error body (graph.threads.net sends Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on errors too, checked after these gradings); start eval 12's success timeout only when that card's iframe actually starts loading.

Problems no assertion caught: eval 12 with skill listed 'post deleted' among the causes of a failed load, copied from the skill's fallback-card text, although a deleted post renders a 'Cannot display thread' card and counts as loaded. The skill's §11.3 fallback-card causes were corrected after this round. Eval 6 without skill silently drops /t/ links, claiming they can't be embedded.
With skill was faster on average and used fewer tokens than without (see run_summary); every configuration ran once, so these averages are rough.

expectations.text: Explains that the CSS min-height on the iframe overrides the inline height embed.js sets, and moves the placeholder to a wrapper (or sets min-height from the reported height) so short posts don't leave a blank band.

ThreadsCard.css:20-27 puts min-height on .threads-card only for idle/queued/loading states; no iframe rule in the CSS; ThreadsCard.jsx:81-82 drops the placeholder variable once loaded/failed.

expectations.text: Explains that embed.js only processes a blockquote once (it swaps the text-post-media class for text-post-media-registered), so retrying or re-showing a post means removing the old iframe and creating a fresh blockquote with the text-post-media class (e.g. a remount with a new key) before calling process() again.
expectations.evidence: response.md:30: 'embed.js 每個 blockquote 只處理一次。處理時，它把 blockquote 的 class 從 `text-post-media` 改成 `text-post-media-registered`'; line 40: '重試或換主題時，丟掉舊的 iframe 和 blockquote，建一個全新的 blockquote 再呼叫 `process()`。' Code: fail() -> teardown removes the stage incl. iframe (threadsEmbed.js:153-157,194-200); retry -> startAttempt -> host.replaceChildren(), then mount builds a new blockquote with class text-post-media and calls api.process() (lines 224-236, 264-266, 110-125). Mock run: after a timeout failure, retry() produced a new iframe and a fresh blockquote that embed.js re-registered, and a later height report set status 'loaded'.

expectations.text: Handles the theme by setting data-theme on the blockquote and re-creating the embed when the site theme changes, since the theme is fixed when embed.js creates the iframe.
expectations.evidence: response.md:46: '主題由 blockquote 的 `data-theme` 決定 ... iframe 一旦建好，主題就固定了'; line 48: '切主題時重建 blockquote 再呼叫 `process()`'. Code: buildBlockquote sets data-theme from config.themeAttribute (threadsEmbed.js:116-117); setTheme starts a swap attempt (lines 286-301); ThreadsCard.jsx:58-61 forwards theme changes. Mock run: setTheme('dark') created a second iframe with '?theme=dark' while keeping the old one, and after the new iframe reported, only the dark iframe remained.

expectations.text: Judges success by the iframe's height postMessage (a number greater than 0, with origin checked against the Threads hosts and event.source matched to that iframe's contentWindow) within a timeout, not by the iframe load event; a 0 report or no report leads to the fallback card.
expectations.evidence: handleMessage checks `config.messageOrigins.includes(event.origin)` (threadsEmbed.js:43; origins https://www.threads.com and https://www.threads.net in threadsEmbedConfig.js:5) and `frame.contentWindow === event.source` (line 48); onReport succeeds only on height > 0 and fails on 0 (lines 219-221); armTimeout fails after reportTimeoutMs = 12000 (lines 159-174). No load listener on the iframe. response.md:63-64 states the same. Mock run: bare number 498 -> 'loaded'; wrong origin, wrong source and object data ignored; 0 -> 'failed' with the host emptied; no report in 12 s -> 'failed', which renders ThreadsFallback (ThreadsCard.jsx:89). Caveat: readHeight (line 38) also accepts digit-only strings (mock: '355' -> 'loaded'), which is looser than 'a number' and contradicts the response's '只認數字', but bare-number reports are handled exactly as the assertion requires.

expectations.text: Builds the blockquote and lets embed.js modify it inside a container element whose children React doesn't render (e.g. created imperatively via a ref), so embed.js inserting the iframe and removing the blockquote doesn't conflict with React's reconciliation (the removeChild errors).

React 不會碰它沒渲染的子節點'.

expectations.text: Gives a working way to find such posts ahead of time that doesn't rely on oEmbed: requesting <permalink>/embed without credentials as a same-origin request from a threads.com page (e.g. a DevTools console snippet, a bookmarklet or an extension content script), where HTTP 500 means login-only and HTTP 200 with class="Embed" in the body means it embeds publicly; a real (headless) browser loading the embed page while logged out also counts. A check that only looks at the HTTP status of a plain server-side request (curl, Node or Python fetch, a CI job) doesn't pass.
expectations.evidence: find-login-only-posts.js:2-4 refuses to run unless location.origin is https://www.threads.com. Line 46 does fetch(`/t/${shortcode}/embed/`, { credentials: 'omit', cache: 'no-store' }). classify (lines 24-35) maps 500 to login-only, 200 + /class="Embed(?:\s[^"]*)?"/ to public, and other 200s to unavailable/deleted. A mocked-fetch run in the grader's scratchpad classified LOGIN1→500 login-only, PUB2→200 public, GONE3→200 unavailable and 429→unexpected, sent relative same-origin requests with credentials 'omit', and threw on a non-threads.com origin. response.md:69 says server-side curl/fetch in Actions cannot tell the posts apart; response.md:87 gives a manual logged-out check (private window opening the /embed/ URL).

expectations.text: Doesn't promise a way to make these posts visible to logged-out visitors (no token, proxy or embed parameter changes that) and doesn't treat them as deleted or remove them from the list.
expectations.evidence: response.md:107: "「只限登入」是 Threads 那邊的判定，嵌入端改不了。" No token, proxy or parameter workaround is offered. The delivered code keeps the posts in the list, marked with data-login-only, and keeps trying to embed them, and response.md:104 says the card "不會說「貼文已刪除」". Borderline: response.md:107 also says "如果這個側欄的目的是讓讀者讀到內容，最實際的做法是換成其他公開貼文；如果這 3 則一定要留，就用 data-login-only". That is a conditional editorial suggestion left to the user. The solution itself does not remove them, so this passes.

notes: Response flags that the numeric height report, HTTP 500 error page and class="Embed" marker are 2026-10 observations, not an official spec
Firefox behavior with partitioned third-party cookies is stated as an untested guess
Headless-browser automation in CI was not tested
User is asked to confirm in Safari/private window, since no live Threads test was run

expectations.text: Gives each blockquote a unique id (e.g. ig-tp-<shortcode>) and explains that embed.js removes the fallback blockquote by that id once the embed reports its height, which is why the 'View on Threads' links stay.
expectations.evidence: The code sets the id (threadsEmbedDom.js:6 `blockquote.id = `ig-tp-${post.code}``), but the explanation does not identify the mechanism. response.md:13-15 lists the missing id as one of three vague 'factors' next to multiple script runs and React/embed.js contention, then says (response.md:16) it could not read embed.js so 'the new component does not depend on its internal behavior'. It hides non-iframe siblings itself (threadsEmbedDom.js:18-27). Nowhere does it say embed.js removes the element whose id matches the blockquote's id when the height report arrives.

expectations.text: Explains that the CSS min-height on the iframe overrides the inline height embed.js sets, and moves the placeholder to a wrapper (or sets min-height from the reported height) so short posts don't leave a blank band.
expectations.evidence: response.md:20: 'embed.js 會依 iframe 內容回報的實際高度設定 iframe 的 `height`，但 `min-height` 的優先權比 `height` 高。結果內容只有 200px 的短貼文，還是被撐到 400px。' response.md:21 moves the reserve to the outer card, active only while not loaded. ThreadsCard.css:12-17 applies min-height only for data-status idle/loading on .threads-card, and ThreadsCard.css:19-22 puts no height or min-height on the iframe.

expectations.text: Explains that embed.js only processes a blockquote once (it swaps the text-post-media class for text-post-media-registered), so retrying or re-showing a post means removing the old iframe and creating a fresh blockquote with the text-post-media class (e.g. a remount with a new key) before calling process() again.
expectations.evidence: response.md:27 says, in general terms, that an already-processed blockquote is not found again and that a retry must remove the old iframe and add a fresh blockquote. It never mentions the text-post-media -> text-post-media-registered swap. It also claims (response.md:25) '`window.instgrm.Embeds.process()` 是 Instagram 的 embed.js 提供的 API，不是 Threads 的', which grader-facts contradicts: process() exists on Threads' embed.js and re-scans. Instead of calling process(), the fix re-inserts the embed.js script (threadsEmbedLoader.js:8-19; response.md:72). Per grader-facts, loading embed.js a second time does not re-scan, so the delivered retry, page change and theme re-creation would not render.

expectations.text: Handles the theme by setting data-theme on the blockquote and re-creating the embed when the site theme changes, since the theme is fixed when embed.js creates the iframe.
expectations.evidence: No data-theme is set anywhere: createBlockquote in threadsEmbedDom.js:3-16 sets only class, id, data-text-post-permalink and data-text-post-version. The response relies on CSS color-scheme instead (ThreadsCard.jsx:44 `style={{ colorScheme: theme }}`) and states (response.md:40) 'Threads 官方嵌入碼沒有文件化的主題參數', which grader-facts contradicts (data-theme -> ?theme=dark|auto). theme is in the effect deps (ThreadsCard.jsx:35), so it does re-create, but without data-theme the result stays light, and the re-creation depends on the script re-insertion that does not re-scan.

expectations.text: Judges success by the iframe's height postMessage (a number greater than 0, with origin checked against the Threads hosts and event.source matched to that iframe's contentWindow) within a timeout, not by the iframe load event; a 0 report or no report leads to the fallback card.
expectations.evidence: No message listener exists in any delivered file (grep for 'message|postMessage' finds only response.md:469, a speculative remark). Success comes from the iframe `load` event plus a ResizeObserver settle timer (threadsEmbedDom.js:50 `iframe.addEventListener('load', handleLoad...)`, :53-63 `setTimeout(() => finish(true), config.settleMs)`). So a login-only post whose /embed/ returns an HTTP 500 page (load fires, no height report) would be marked ready and shown as an empty iframe.

expectations.text: Builds the blockquote and lets embed.js modify it inside a container element whose children React doesn't render (e.g. created imperatively via a ref), so embed.js inserting the iframe and removing the blockquote doesn't conflict with React's reconciliation (the removeChild errors).
expectations.evidence: ThreadsCard.jsx:47 renders `<div ref={mountRef} className="threads-card__mount" hidden={status === 'error'} />` with no React children. The blockquote is built imperatively (threadsEmbedDom.js:3-16, :35 `mount.replaceChildren(createBlockquote(...))`) and cleaned up with replaceChildren on dispose (:86-90). The fallback is a React sibling, not inside the mount. response.md:28-30 explains that the removeChild errors come from React and embed.js both touching the same nodes, and gives this as the fix.

expectations.text: Loads embed.js once for the whole app (e.g. a shared module-level promise or a single script tag), not once per card.
expectations.evidence: threadsEmbedLoader.js:3-23 only merges requests made in the same microtask. pendingScan is reset to null (line 7), and every later request appends a new `<script src=embed.js>` and removes it after load. response.md:72: '需要掃描時，插入一個新的 `<script src=".../embed.js">`...一頁 10 張卡片只執行一次'. That is once per batch: every page change, retry, theme change and IntersectionObserver-delayed card adds another script tag, not one load per app. Per grader-facts, those reloads also do not re-scan.

expectations.text: The fallback card links only to validated https://www.threads.com or https://www.threads.net post URLs and is built without inserting untrusted strings via innerHTML or dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
expectations.evidence: threadsUrl.js:11-20 requires the https: protocol, a hostname in [threads.com, www.threads.com, threads.net, www.threads.net] and the path /@user/post/code, then rebuilds the permalink as `https://www.threads.com/@${username}/post/${code}`. A bun test of this parser returned null for http://, javascript:, evil.com, www.threads.com.evil.com and a path containing quote/HTML characters, and the canonical threads.com URL for valid input. The fallback uses JSX `href={post.permalink}` and text children (ThreadsCard.jsx:48-60). The blockquote link uses textContent (threadsEmbedDom.js:13). Neither innerHTML nor dangerouslySetInnerHTML appears in the delivered code.

expectations.text: Points out that a deleted or unavailable post still renders a 'Cannot display thread' card that reports a height, so client-side success detection counts it as loaded, and recommends pruning such posts with the oEmbed endpoint (code 24 means gone), e.g. on the backend or in a scheduled job.
expectations.evidence: Partially covered. response.md:44 says onload still fires for deleted posts. response.md:51 says the frontend cannot tell them apart ('Threads 會在 iframe 裡顯示它自己的提示') and recommends a backend check at entry time plus a scheduled re-check 'using the Threads oEmbed endpoint'. But it never says that the 'Cannot display thread' card reports a height, and it never says how to read the oEmbed result: no mention of code 24 (or the HTTP 400) as the 'gone' signal. It only says '失效的網址就不要回給前端', which leaves transient errors and rate limits indistinguishable from deletions.

expectations.text: Identifies the three posts as ones Threads shows only to logged-in users (e.g. marked sensitive): visitors who aren't logged in to Threads, or whose browser blocks third-party cookies (Safari and private windows do by default), get Meta's error page, while a logged-in viewer who allows third-party cookies (like the author in Chrome) sees them.
expectations.evidence: response.md:5 says the 3 posts are not dead, they are posts you can't see without logging in ("沒登入就看不到的貼文"). Lines 7-8 say the author's normal Chrome sends threads.com third-party cookies into the iframe so it loads as the logged-in author, while Safari (ITP) and Chrome incognito block third-party cookies, so the iframe is always logged out and gets Meta's "Sorry, something went wrong" page, "就算讀者在 Safari 有登入 Threads，嵌入裡還是未登入". Line 37 names sensitive or age-restricted content as the most common cause. Lines 36-38 also hedge with other causes (replies in private threads, archived posts), but the main diagnosis matches.

expectations.text: States that oEmbed still returns embed HTML (HTTP 200) for such posts, so the weekly oEmbed check can't flag them; oEmbed's code 24 only catches posts that are gone.
expectations.evidence: response.md:17 says the oEmbed html is a fixed blockquote plus script, not a rendered result, and that a 200 only means the URL maps to a post; "這支 API 不會告訴你沒登入的人能不能看". Line 19 says the check is still useful because it catches deleted posts and mistyped URLs ("抓得到刪文、網址打錯"), and line 103 says oEmbed catches deletions while the new check catches logged-out visibility. Code 24 is never named, but the substance is there. A side claim is wrong: line 17 says oEmbed is queried with the user's access token and returns 200 because 'your token's identity can see it'. Per the facts, oEmbed needs no token and returns 200 for login-only posts anyway.

expectations.text: Explains why the current success check passes on the error page: the error page still loads from www.threads.com, and the CSS min-height on the iframe makes the height test pass regardless of what the frame shows.
expectations.evidence: response.md:26 says the error page comes back from that same URL, so the src doesn't change. Line 27 says the 8-second height check measures the iframe element's layout height and that `.sidebar-threads iframe { min-height: 300px; }` keeps it at 300px or more. Both required parts are present. Line 27 also claims that without the rule the iframe would default to 150px and still pass. That is false: embed.js inserts the iframe at height 0, so min-height is what makes the test pass. Line 25 says embed.js replaces the blockquote right away, but embed.js only removes the blockquote when a height report arrives.

expectations.text: Rewrites success detection around the embed page's height postMessage: a numeric report greater than 0, with event.origin checked against the Threads hosts and event.source matched to that iframe, within a timeout; the error page sends no report, so it ends in the fallback. Iframe presence, its src or its rendered height are not treated as success.
expectations.evidence: The origin check (js/threads-sidebar.js:153), the event.source match (:157) and the timeouts (js/threads-embed-core.js:109-127) are present. But the handler only accepts an Instagram-style `{type:"MEASURE",details:{height}}` object or JSON string (js/threads-embed-core.js:78-84; response.md:54). The real report is a bare number. I replayed it through the delivered sidebar flow using the run's own fake DOM: a message with data 498 from https://www.threads.com, sent by the good post's iframe, gives readMeasuredHeight(498) === null. The good post then ends in state 'card' with reason load-failed instead of 'ok'. So every public embed would also be replaced by the fallback card. Success also needs height >= 120 (minMeasuredHeight), not > 0.

expectations.text: Moves the placeholder height off the iframe (e.g. to a wrapper) or drops it, since a CSS min-height on the iframe overrides the height embed.js sets.
expectations.evidence: response.md:68 says to delete `.sidebar-threads iframe { min-height: 300px; }`; the wrapper keeps 300px only while data-state="loading". css/threads-sidebar.css:23-30 has no iframe min-height and puts `min-height: var(--threads-slot-reserve)` on `.threads-slot[data-state="loading"]`. The response never says that a CSS min-height overrides embed.js's height, but the required change is made.

expectations.text: Shows a fallback card for these posts that links to the post on Threads and says the post needs both a Threads login and third-party cookies allowed in the browser (a card that mentions only logging in fails, since a logged-in Safari or private-window visitor still can't see it), doesn't call the post deleted, and keeps trying to load these posts in the page because logged-in visitors can see them.
expectations.evidence: The card links to the post (js/threads-sidebar.js:93-106) and doesn't call it deleted. But the login-required text, threads-embeds.json:17, mentions only logging in: "Threads 只開放登入的使用者看這則貼文，點上面的連結登入後就能看到完整內容。" It says nothing about third-party cookies. The response also recommends not embedding these posts at all: response.md:107 "已知要登入才看得到的，就不要嵌入", using `display: card`. createSlot (js/threads-sidebar.js:50-52) then never tries to load them, so logged-in visitors can't see them either.

expectations.text: Gives a working way to find such posts ahead of time that doesn't rely on oEmbed: requesting <permalink>/embed without credentials as a same-origin request from a threads.com page (e.g. a DevTools console snippet, a bookmarklet or an extension content script), where HTTP 500 means login-only and HTTP 200 with class="Embed" in the body means it embeds publicly; a real (headless) browser loading the embed page while logged out also counts. A check that only looks at the HTTP status of a plain server-side request (curl, Node or Python fetch, a CI job) doesn't pass.
expectations.evidence: response.md:76 gives a manual check: copy the embed iframe's src from DevTools Elements and open it in an incognito or Safari private window; "看到「Sorry, something went wrong」就是這種貼文". That is a real logged-out browser loading the /embed page, which per the facts returns Meta's error page for login-only posts. So it is a working way that doesn't rely on oEmbed. The console probe (scripts/devtools-probe.js) also tells them apart, since it logs any threads.com message, though it says to look for MEASURE. The Playwright CI check, which the response calls the most reliable method (line 48), does not work: it parses heights with the same MEASURE parser. A mocked public post with bare-number reports 534 and 574 plus author text classifies as blocked/no-measure. The control post would therefore fail and the run would exit 2 as 'untrusted'. This pass rests on the manual tip only.

expectations.text: Doesn't promise a way to make these posts visible to logged-out visitors (no token, proxy or embed parameter changes that) and doesn't treat them as deleted or remove them from the list.
expectations.evidence: No token, proxy or embed-parameter fix is proposed. response.md:5 says "那 3 則沒有失效". The cards use a separate login-required reason, not a deleted one (threads-embeds.json:16-19), and the sample config keeps the login-only post in the list as a card (threads-embeds.json:28-33). Borderline: response.md:108 offers, as an opt-in for an all-embed sidebar, to swap the 3 posts for other public posts, or to repost if the cause is a reply in a private thread. The default handling keeps them listed.

notes: Round 10 checks the 2026-10-24 additions: posts Threads shows only to logged-in users (§11.1, §11.2, §11.3, §12), counting only numeric height reports, and the fallback-card causes. It runs the new eval 13 (a blog sidebar where three login-only posts show Meta's error page to logged-out readers) and reruns eval 12 as a regression check. Same conditions as round 9: no internet, no browser tools; none of the runs reported using them.
With skill passes 17/17 (100% averaged per eval), without skill 9/17 (54%): eval 12 9/9 vs 3/9, eval 13 8/8 vs 6/8.

Eval 13 with skill identifies the login-only posts, explains why oEmbed and the old check miss them, counts only numeric height reports, keeps trying to load these posts and shows a card that names both the Threads login and third-party cookies, and finds such posts ahead of time with a same-origin, credential-less /embed check from a threads.com page (the grader confirmed 500 / 200 with class="Embed" / 200 without it are classified correctly).

Eval 13 discriminates less than evals 6, 11 and 12: 6 of its 8 assertions pass in both configurations. Without the skill the model still worked out the logged-in / third-party-cookie cause, the oEmbed blind spot, why the old check passed, the min-height fix and a manual private-window check. It loses on the height report (its listener only accepts an Instagram-style {type: 'MEASURE', details: {height}} object, so the grader's bare-number 498 was ignored and every working embed would turn into a fallback card) and on the page handling (it stops embedding the login-only posts and its card mentions only logging in). It also wrongly says oEmbed's 200 depends on an access token.

Eval 12 with skill passes all 9 again; its fallback card no longer lists 'post deleted' and names rate limiting, blockers, network problems and login-only posts / blocked third-party cookies, matching the corrected §11.3. Without skill repeats rounds 8 and 9: process() called Instagram-only, re-inserting embed.js to re-scan, no theme parameter, success by load plus ResizeObserver.

Grader suggestions: in eval 13, say in assertion 7 whether a manual 'open it in a private window' tip is enough or require the recommended detection method to classify public and login-only posts correctly (the without-skill Playwright check has the same format bug and would mark public posts as failed); say in assertion 8 whether suggesting replacement counts as removal; add an assertion that deleted posts (a ~194 px 'Cannot display thread' card) pass height detection and still need oEmbed code 24. In eval 12, add an assertion on the fallback card's stated causes and a separate one that re-scanning goes through window.instgrm.Embeds.process() and that process() isn't called Instagram-only.
